info.title: Ductura API
info.description:
Shared errors: any route may answer these besides the errors listed under it.
- 500 internal: problem body {error, code, messageKey: "errors.internal", status, requestId}.
- 429 too_many_requests: problem body {error, code, messageKey: "errors.tooManyRequests", status, requestId}; header retry-after in whole seconds.
- 401 session_idle_expired: problem body {error, code, messageKey: "errors.sessionIdleExpired", status, requestId}.

get.summary: The analyses the server can calculate, each with its id, its version and which columns it takes (numeric only, or any), and the limits of a dataset: rows, columns, characters in a category cell and bytes of a request. Titles and descriptions are not in the answer; the client names the ids. While the function is off the answer is 404 not_found.

post.summary: Calculates one analysis over the dataset in the body: descriptive statistics (n, missing, mean, sample standard deviation, median, minimum, quartiles, maximum), a frequency table, or Pearson correlation with pairwise deletion of missing cells. Nothing is stored and the dataset and the result are not written to any record. Numbers are rounded to 6 decimals; a value that is not defined is null. The same analysisVersion over the same dataset (same rows, same column order) gives the same result, datasetSha256 and resultSha256, byte for byte; the order of the rows does not change the result. A version the server no longer holds is 422 unknown_analysis_version. A dataset outside the limits of the catalogue, a repeated column or variable name, a row with a different number of cells than there are columns, an unknown variable or a column of the wrong kind is 422 invalid_input. While the function is off the answer is 404 not_found.
OIDC back-channel logout: the provider posts a signed logout token, no cookie.

get.summary: Return from the identity provider; checks state and PKCE, opens the session.
Starts AAI@EduHr login (PKCE); returnTo is narrowed to a safe local path.

post.summary: Closes every session of the caller; on failure keeps the cookie.
Closes the current session. Same Origin only; an empty body.
Confirms the caller's security key against an assertion challenge. 403 for a key that is not the caller's or is revoked; 409 when the signature counter fell or stayed the same (0 to 0 is accepted).

400.description: content_length_invalid, content_length_mismatch, body_stream_error, invalid_json, challenge_invalid, ceremony_invalid

post.summary: A one-time challenge of 32 random bytes for one ceremony of this session, registration or assertion. It expires after timeoutMs and is spent by the first attempt, successful or not.

200.description: challenge issued; the purpose picks the shape

post.summary: Registers the caller's security key (ES256, COSE -7; attestation none) against a registration challenge; the key is the COSE key in authenticatorData. 403 when the account already has a key, 409 when the key is registered.

400.description: content_length_invalid, content_length_mismatch, body_stream_error, invalid_json, challenge_invalid, ceremony_invalid

post.summary: Records the client's environment (D-300): app, version, system, browser, device and a screen width class, each from a closed list. Works without a login, under the rate limit; the body is the JCS form of the value, and any other field, value or form is 400 invalid_input. Never used to decide access.

Records that the web met an error nobody caught (DAN-1568): its kind, its class, the page of the app and the app's version, each from a closed list. No message, stack, address or typed value can be sent. Works without a login, under the rate limit; the body is the JCS form of the value, and any other field, value or form is 400 invalid_input. Never used to decide access.

Comments on a work (B-10). The action picks the body: create {anchor, body, documentId} and reply {body, threadId} answer 200 {id}; resolve and reopen {threadId} and delete {commentId} answer 204; list {documentId} answers 200 {comments}. Exactly those keys, at most 16 KiB; an unknown action is 404. The database decides who may read or write (403); a thread that changed in the meantime is 409.

revision.description: The revision of the work the thread is written on: required of a teacher, optional for the owning student. It must exist for the document and be one the caller may read (a teacher's: up to the newest standing submission, or the current revision before there is one; not only the newest); otherwise 422.

The revision of the work the thread is written on: required of a teacher, optional for the owning student. It must exist for the document and be one the caller may read (a teacher's: up to the newest standing submission, or the current revision before there is one; not only the newest); otherwise 422.

200.description: the new comment's id (create, reply) or the comments (list)

revision.description: The revision of the work the thread was written on; a reply has its thread's. Null for a thread written before revisions were recorded.
The revision of the work the thread was written on; a reply has its thread's. Null for a thread written before revisions were recorded.

post.summary: Revision requests on a work (DAN-314). The action picks the body, as its exact JCS bytes, at most 16 KiB: create {anchor, documentId, instruction, requestedRevision} answers 200 {request_id, row_seq, version, state}; respond, accept, reopen, rereview and withdraw (with requestId and expectedSeq) answer 200 {outcome: "applied", row_seq, version, state}, or 409 {outcome: "conflict", row_seq, version, state} when expectedSeq is stale; list {documentId} answers 200 {requests}. A malformed id reads as a foreign one (403); a transition the state does not allow is 409 not_allowed; an unknown action is 404.

409.description: expectedSeq is stale: the current counter, version and state; not_allowed

post.summary: The student owner of a work sends the revision to the teacher for review (BLOK ED-43): the body is the exact JCS bytes of {documentId, message}, the message to the teacher a revision text or null. The answer is 200 {round}, the next round of the work (1, 2, 3 ...). A round needs a revision request opened or reopened since the previous round, so a repeated send never skips a round: 409 not_allowed otherwise, also on a submitted work. The teacher of the work is 403; anybody else, an unknown work and a malformed id are 404.

The student owner accepts a pending suggestion (ED-42): {suggestionId}, at most 1 KiB. The server applies it to the current live state and answers 200 {suggestionId, state: "accepted", baseHash, text, change}: text is the exact JCS bytes of the new document for the student's own live.document.put, baseHash the live state it was applied to, change the recorded change with source "teacher-suggestion". Nothing else is written: the work changes only with that put. A suggestion decided before, one whose quote no longer stands in the live state and a submitted work are 409 and the suggestion stays as it was; a teacher of the work is 403; another's and an unknown suggestion are 404.

200.description: the accepted suggestion applied to the live state

post.summary: The student owner rejects a pending suggestion (ED-42): {suggestionId}, at most 1 KiB; 204. The work does not change. A suggestion decided before and a submitted work are 409; a teacher of the work is 403; another's and an unknown suggestion are 404.

The text suggestions of a work (ED-42), the same rows for its student owner and every teacher of it, oldest first, at most 500: {suggestions: [{suggestionId, anchor, text, state, isOwn, baseHash, createdWindow, decidedWindow}]}. state is pending, accepted or rejected; isOwn marks a teacher's own suggestion and is false for the student; baseHash is the live state the suggestion was made on; times are in the 5-minute window of P-03. The body is {documentId}, at most 1 KiB. Another's, an unknown and a malformed work are 404.

A teacher of a work suggests a text for an anchored quote of its live state (ED-42): {documentId, anchor, text}, at most 16 KiB; an empty text removes the quote, a text equal to the quote is 422. The anchor must still select exactly that quote in the live state the teacher reads (a teacher's read writes the access log). 200 {suggestionId, baseHash}. The work does not change: only its student owner can accept. A state that changed meanwhile, a work with nothing published, a submitted work and a work with 500 suggestions are 409; the student owner is 403; another's, an unknown and a malformed work are 404.

200.description: the new suggestion and the live state it was made on

get.summary: Whole-course snapshot for a course teacher. A student counts once at the furthest work stage. Started includes submitted. Suppresses all counts for fewer than five students, incomplete course access, or any nonempty stage below five. No filters.

The desktop packages a client may offer: one row per system and architecture at most, by system then architecture. url is a path on this address or an https address; sha256 is the SHA-256 of the package bytes in lowercase hex, which the client checks before it opens the package. An empty list: no package yet. A manifest the server cannot read makes the answer 503, never a partial list.

200.description: manifest (an empty list when there is no package yet)

post.summary: One evidence segment and the document after it. Same Origin, `ductus-protocol: 1` (signed now, 200) or `2` (signed by the worker: 202 pending_signature, then the same request again).

202.description: stored, receipt pending_signature (protocol 2 only); not an acknowledgement

post.summary: The caller's own work for one assignment and its current revision; `start: true` makes it. Same Origin, `ductus-protocol: 1`; anyone but the student gets 404.

One page of the replay of a work: the verified stored bytes of its segments in chain order, as the JCS text of the page. The body is exactly {documentId, from: 0} for the first page and {documentId, from, head} for every later one, with the head the first page reported; any other shape is 422. Same Origin, `ductus-protocol: 1`. A work the caller may not read, an id that cannot exist or a page past the end is 404. A record that no longer ends at `head` is 409 record_changed (read again from the first page); a record that does not verify is 503, never a partial page.

200.description: one page, its JCS text unchanged

get.summary: The academic years in which the session's institution has a course, newest first, for its administrator. No query; any query is 422. Anyone who is not a confirmed administrator is 403.

post.summary: The student acknowledges the notice of an assignment version they were shown. The body is exactly {versionNo, fingerprint}: the version and the SHA-256 the browser computed of the notice text, at most 1 KiB, sent as application/json (charset utf-8 only), with no escape and no repeated key. A malformed assignment id is 400 invalid_assignment_id, judged before the session. A version that is no longer current is 409 conflict; a stored notice other than the one shown is 409 notice_changed, and nothing is recorded.

get.summary: The log of administrator and operator actions in the caller's institution, newest first, at most 500 (truncated says more exist): roles confirmed or revoked, rules published, thresholds changed, legal holds placed or released, data exports requested or approved. Each entry has the time, the acting role, the kind of action, the role it concerns and the outcome, and no person, student, work or case. Read only; a caller who is not a confirmed administrator is 403.

The courses of the session's institution in one academic year (exactly one academicYear=YYYY/YYYY, the second year the first plus one), for its administrator: by name (hr collation), then id, each with its number of open students, its holder, its team and its groups (each with its open students and teachers); people by family and given name (hr collation), then id, those without a name last. No student is named. Any other query is 422; anyone who is not a confirmed administrator is 403.

post.summary: An administrator of the institution creates a course: exactly {name, academicYear, aiPolicy, holderId, groups}, at most 8 KiB, sent as application/json (charset utf-8 only). holderId is a confirmed teacher of the same institution, who becomes the course's holder and a teacher of it; groups are the names of its seminar groups (0 to 20, distinct, each 1 to 80 UTF-16 units with no space at either end). The name is 1 to 160 UTF-16 units with no space at either end; the academic year is two consecutive years such as 2026/2027. A teacher who is not an administrator is 403. The same course (institution, academic year, name) sent again with the same content answers its id; with other content it is 409 conflict.

put.summary: The teacher of the assignment says whether a submission after its deadline is allowed, exactly {lateSubmissionAllowed}; allowed by default. It may change after publication; setting the value in force changes nothing and returns it. A body that is not exactly this is 422. A student, another teacher, an unknown or a malformed assignment returns 404.

get.summary: The setting in force for the assignment. An assignment that never had one reads as teams off (enabled false, minSize 2, maxSize 6, student_choice). Read by the teachers of the course; another's, an unknown or a malformed assignment reads 404.

put.summary: The teacher of the course sets whether the assignment is done in teams, the fewest and the most members (2 to 6, minSize not above maxSize) and who forms the teams: the students or the teacher. Each call adds a version; the last one counts. With teams on, every member does their own part. A setting that would leave an existing team above maxSize is 409 conflict. An assignment that is another's, unknown or malformed reads 404.

post.summary: A teacher of the assignment publishes its next version against the version they saw: {expectedVersion} and the whole content, both word bounds named (null drops one), at most 90 000 bytes. A tightening of the rules, an AI purpose under a prohibited policy, wordMin above wordMax or an impossible date is 422; a stale version is 409 version_conflict, and of two requests with the same version one writes.

get.summary: The current version of an assignment, for a teacher of its course: its number and whole content as institution.assignment-versions.post takes it, instants as Date.toISOString writes them. groupIds, externalToolsAllowed and aiSummaryOnly are those of the creation, absent until the server stores them. Sec-Fetch-Site, when sent, other than same-origin is 403; a malformed id is 422; another course's assignment, an unknown one and any caller who is not a teacher of its course are the same 404 (C-23). A row the read cannot vouch for makes the whole answer 503.

An administrator of the institution reads the daily number of assistant requests per student and assignment of the own institution, as {version, limit}: version is the latest version of the institution's cost configuration (0 when none), limit null when none is set. A number of requests, never an amount. A teacher, a student and an account without a confirmed role are 403.

put.summary: Only an administrator of the institution sets the daily number of assistant requests per student and assignment of the own institution: exactly {expectedVersion, limit}, limit a positive integer or null to remove it. expectedVersion is the latest version the administrator saw (0 when none); another version added in between is 409 conflict, and the same change sent again returns the version it made. Every other value of the cost configuration stays. Answers 200 with {version, limit} in force. The new version is recorded in the audit trail in the same transaction. A body that is not exactly this is 422. A teacher, a student and an account without a confirmed role are 403. The institution and the author come from the session, never from the body.

get.summary: The assistant setting of the caller's faculty for a confirmed administrator of its institution, read only: assistant (the assistant answers on this server; no provider or model is ever named), the two flags of the faculty switch (transcription, tools) from the versioned faculty setting, its settingVersion (null when the faculty has no setting: both flags off) and changeable, always false: the switch changes only through the owner's PR, never from a screen (OC-1). No query: any query parameter is 422. A teacher, a student and an account without a confirmed administrator role are 403.

200.description: the assistant setting of the faculty

post.summary: An administrator of the institution adds the next version of its rules: exactly {expectedVersion, citationStyle, workLanguages, defaultWorkLanguage}, at most 4 KiB, sent as application/json. expectedVersion is the latest version the administrator saw (0 when none); another version added in between is 409 conflict. The rules are citationStyle: fpzg, workLanguages: a non-empty set of hr and en, and defaultWorkLanguage: one of workLanguages; anything else, including an unknown key and a default language that is not offered, is 422 invalid_input. A teacher, a student and an account without a confirmed role are 403. The institution and the author come from the session, never from the body. The new version is recorded in the audit trail in the same transaction. Success follows the database commit.

get.summary: The rules of the caller's institution for an administrator of it: current is the latest version, or null while the institution has none, and versions is the whole history in ascending order of version. Each version is {version, effectiveFrom, rules}. No query. A teacher, a student and an account without a confirmed role in the institution are 403.

200.description: the current version and the history

post.summary: A teacher of the course creates and publishes an assignment (version 1) with its rules on AI tools (aiPolicy and aiPurposes, A-14): {requestKey} and the whole content, at most 90 000 bytes, sent as application/json (charset utf-8 only). requestKey is a UUID the client makes once per form, in the body so the generated client sends it. The same key with the same content answers the same id; with other content it is 409 conflict. A malformed course id or key, a tightening the course forbids, an AI purpose under a prohibited policy, wordMin above wordMax or an impossible date is 422. Publishing sends nothing to anyone (C-17): students see it in student.assignments.get. Optional: groupIds, the course's seminar groups it is for (absent or empty: the whole course); externalToolsAllowed (outside tools, absent false); aiSummaryOnly (the AI assistant only summarises, absent false). A group of another course or one named twice, and aiSummaryOnly under a prohibited policy or with any aiPurposes, are 422.

A teacher of the course team or an administrator of the institution assigns a confirmed teacher of the institution to a seminar group: exactly {teacherId}, at most 1 KiB. The teacher joins the course team through the group. assigned is false when they already teach the group. A teacher who is not confirmed is 422.

get.summary: The seminar groups of a course, for a teacher of its team or an administrator of its institution: by name (hr collation), then id, each with its open teachers (by family and given name, hr collation, then id) and the number of its open students; no student is named. A malformed course id is 422. Another institution's course and an unknown one are the same 403 (C-23).

post.summary: The holder, a collaborator of the course team (C-7) or an administrator of the institution adds a seminar group: exactly {name}, 1 to 80 UTF-16 units with no space at either end, at most 1 KiB. A group of the same name answers its id; nothing is made twice. A student is 403.

A teacher creates a course in their institution: exactly {name, academicYear, aiPolicy}, at most 2 KiB, sent as application/json (only the media type before any parameter is judged). The name is 1 to 160 UTF-16 units with no space at either end; the academic year is two consecutive years such as 2026/2027. The same course sent again answers its id, never a second course.
A teacher of the course revokes its enrolment code. The body is exactly {}; revoked is false when there was no code to revoke.

get.summary: Whether the course has an enrolment code, for a teacher of the course: current is the code last issued and not revoked, with its validUntil (Date.toISOString), or null when none was issued or it was revoked. A current code past validUntil is still current: the client shows it as expired. The code itself is never sent (A-8). Sec-Fetch-Site, when sent, other than same-origin is 403; a malformed id is 422; another institution's course, an unknown one and any caller who is not a teacher of the course are the same 404 (C-23).

post.summary: A teacher of the course issues its enrolment code, valid until {validUntil}, replacing any earlier one; at most 1 KiB. The instant keeps its offset and fraction as sent; an impossible date or one the database refuses is 422.

Enrols the caller in the course of a code. The body is exactly {code}, at most 64 UTF-16 units and 1 KiB, sent as application/json (charset utf-8 only). A wrong or expired code is 422 refused; too many guesses are 429 too_many_attempts, and each guess counts even when refused.

get.summary: The faculty rules of the caller's institution for an administrator of it: one entry per work type, in the fixed order of work types, each with its published versions in ascending order of versionNo (an empty list when none is published). No query: any query parameter is 422. A teacher, a student and an account without a confirmed administrator role are 403.

200.description: the rule versions per work type

post.summary: An administrator of the institution publishes the next version of the rules of one work type: exactly {workType, basedOnVersionNo, aiPolicy, aiPurposes, evidenceProfile, importAllowed}, at most 4 KiB, sent as application/json. basedOnVersionNo is the latest version the administrator saw, or null when none is published; another version published in between is 409 conflict. Purposes are a set of at most five and none with the policy prohibited; a value outside the closed lists or a purpose with the prohibited policy is 422 (invalid_work_type, invalid_ai_policy, invalid_ai_purposes, invalid_evidence_profile, or invalid_input for any other shape). A teacher, a student and an account without a confirmed administrator role are 403. The institution, the author and the time come from the session and the database clock, never from the body. The version is recorded in the audit trail in the same transaction. Success follows the database commit.

get.summary: The courses of the TRIAL ISVU source of the caller's institution for an administrator (val 22). The source is an invented one with invented courses and students, not ISVU and not any interface of Srce; nothing leaves the server. Query: exactly academicYear (for example 2026/2027), any other parameter or a missing or malformed value is 422. Answer: mode (always mock) and the courses of that year, each with its sourceCourseKey, name, academicYear and enrolledCount (the number of students the source lists; no names). Only an administrator of the institution (403 otherwise). When the institution's ISVU setting is off, which is the default and always the case in production, the answer is the ordinary 404 not_found, so the integration is not revealed.

200.description: the courses of the trial source

post.summary: Step one of the import of a course's students from the TRIAL ISVU source (val 22): the preview. Exactly {sourceCourseKey} as application/json, at most 1 KiB. The server reads the students of that course from the trial source and previews them as institution.roster-imports.post previews a file, with the same answer (source is isvu; the lines count from 2): every row is new, already_enrolled or unsuitable with a reason, matched to an account only by its AAI@EduHr identifier, never by name. Nothing is enrolled. importId confirms it with institution.roster-import-confirm.post until expiresAt (30 minutes), as for a file. A sourceCourseKey the source does not know, a course that is not the institution's and an institution whose ISVU setting is off (the default, and always in production) are the ordinary 404 not_found; a body that is not exactly a valid key is 422. Only an administrator of the institution (403 otherwise).

A second administrator releases a legal hold with a reason: exactly {reason}, 1 to 600 characters, at most 2 KiB, sent as application/json. The administrator who placed the hold, and a caller who is not an administrator, get 403. A missing hold or one of another institution is 404; a hold already released is 409; a malformed id or reason is 422 (an id that is not a UUID is 404).

get.summary: The legal holds of the caller's institution, standing and released, for a confirmed administrator. A caller who is not an administrator is 403.

post.summary: An administrator places a legal hold on a work, a student or an assignment of the institution: exactly {subjectType, subjectId, caseReference}, at most 2 KiB, sent as application/json. A caller who is not an administrator is 403; a subject outside the institution is 404; an invalid reference is 422.

get.summary: The template of milestones of the caller's institution for an administrator of it: current is the latest version, or null while there is none, and versions is the whole history in ascending order. Each version is {version, effectiveFrom, requireFinalStageApproval, milestones}, a milestone being {title, relativeDue?, submits}. No query. A teacher, a student and an account without a confirmed role are 403.

200.description: the current version and the history

put.summary: An administrator of the institution replaces its template of milestones with a new version: exactly {expectedVersion, requireFinalStageApproval, milestones}, at most 16 KiB, sent as application/json. expectedVersion is the latest version the administrator saw (0 when none); another version added in between is 409 conflict. At most 20 milestones, each {title, relativeDue?, submits}: a title of 1 to 200 characters, relativeDue a whole number of days from 1 to 1095 after a work is made, submits topic_text or current_version; anything else is 422 invalid_input. requireFinalStageApproval says whether the final submission waits for the approval of the last milestone; false is the default and the final submission is independent of it. Works that already have their milestones keep them. A teacher, a student and an account without a confirmed role are 403. The institution and the author come from the session, never from the body.

delete.summary: An administrator of the institution removes the threshold of one kind of origin; the kind has none from then on and nothing is compared for it. 204 also when the kind had none (nothing is recorded then). No body. A kind outside the closed list is 422. A teacher, a student and an account without a confirmed administrator role are 403. The removal is recorded in the audit trail in the same transaction.

put.summary: An administrator of the institution sets the threshold of one kind of origin: exactly {thresholdPercent, strictness}, at most 1 KiB, sent as application/json. The kind comes from the path and is one of the closed list; the threshold is a whole percent, 0 to 100, and strictness is hard or soft. changed is false when the kind already held exactly this and nothing is recorded. A kind outside the list, a value outside these or a malformed body is 422. A teacher, a student and an account without a confirmed administrator role are 403. The institution, the author and the time come from the session and the database clock. The change is recorded in the audit trail in the same transaction. Success follows the database commit.

get.summary: The thresholds of the caller's institution per kind of origin, for an administrator of it: at most one per kind of the closed list, in the order of the list, an empty list while the faculty has written none (there are no defaults). No query: any query parameter is 422. A teacher, a student and an account without a confirmed administrator role are 403.

The dry run of retention for an administrator of the institution of the session: per data class (sessions, live view state, versions, time per change, access log, hashes and receipts) its message key, its period in days or null while undecided (D-30), its mode, how many rows a deletion would take and the time of the last deletion run. A class with a null period is always dry-run. Hashes and receipts are never deleted and never counted (candidates null); a class without storage of its own has null candidates. Nothing is deleted or written. A teacher, a student or an administrator of another institution is 403. No query.

periodStatus.description: decided: retentionDays is a number; awaiting_decision: retentionDays is null because the faculty has not set the period yet (none is ever made up); never_deleted: the class proves a submission and is never deleted.

post.summary: An administrator of the institution confirms one candidate as a teacher. The body is exactly {}. A caller who is not an administrator is 403; for an administrator every candidate that cannot be confirmed (themself, another institution's, a missing one, one whose last login gave no right) is the same 404.

An administrator of the institution ends one person's confirmed teacher role. The body is exactly {}; revoked is false when that person holds no active confirmed teacher role in the caller's institution, so another institution's person looks the same as a missing one.

Step two of the import of a course's students (NF-7 OA-10): exactly {} as application/json. The administrator confirms a preview of institution.roster-imports.post; its new rows are enrolled as students of the course, each as enrolment by code would. A student who became a member meanwhile counts as alreadyEnrolled, one a teacher removed meanwhile as skipped. Confirmed again, by any administrator of the institution, it answers its first result with alreadyConfirmed true and enrols nobody twice. A preview past its expiry is 410 import_expired (preview the file again); an import that is not the institution's is 404. Only an administrator of the institution (403 otherwise).

Step one of the import of a course's students from Merlin or ISVU (NF-7 OA-10): the preview. Exactly {source, csv} as application/json, at most 256 KiB; source is merlin or isvu, csv the file's text, at most 200 000 UTF-16 units and 1000 rows after the header. The format is a proposal waiting for a real export: a header with identifikator (AAI@EduHr identifier), ime and prezime in any case and order, other columns ignored, semicolon or comma, RFC 4180 quotes. Every row answers its line, its cells as the file has them (trimmed, identifier in lower case) and a status: new (an account of the institution, to enrol), already_enrolled, or unsuitable with a reason (invalid_identifier, missing_name, duplicate of an earlier row, unknown_account (no account of the institution: the student has not signed in yet), ineligible_account (an account the import never enrols; it enrols by code), name_mismatch, removed from the course by a teacher, course_teacher). Nothing is enrolled. importId confirms it with institution.roster-import-confirm.post until expiresAt (30 minutes). A file without the three columns is 422 roster_columns_missing, more rows than allowed 422 roster_too_many_rows, a quote left open 422 roster_malformed. Only an administrator of the institution (403 otherwise); a course that is not the institution's is 404.

get.summary: For each data export the caller may see, the person it is for and its state, newest first: every request of the institution for a clerk of the registry office or an administrator, the caller's own for anyone else, never another institution's (someone else's request is absent, as one that does not exist). Only exportId, studentId and state.

200.description: the person and state of each export, possibly none

post.summary: A confirmed administrator of the institution, who is neither the clerk who requested nor the person, starts the job with its reference: exactly {reference}, 1 to 120 characters, at most 2 KiB, as application/json. Anyone else is 403; a request of another institution, or an id that is not a UUID, is 404; a request no longer waiting is 409; an invalid reference is 422.

200.description: the job is approved; the worker prepares the package

get.summary: The data exports the caller may see, newest first: every request of the institution for a clerk of the registry office or an administrator, the caller's own for anyone else, never another institution's. The link token is never returned; expiresAt is null until the package is ready.

post.summary: A clerk of the registry office requests the export of the data of a student or a former student of the institution and confirms that the identity was checked: exactly {studentId, identityCheckedBy, note}, identityCheckedBy one of identity_card, passport, student_card, note the reference of the check (1 to 80 characters, never a document number), at most 2 KiB, as application/json. A caller who is not a clerk, a clerk who is also an administrator, and a clerk for themselves are 403; a person outside the institution is 404; an open request for the person is 409; an invalid note is 422.

reason.description: An open request (requested, approved or ready) for the same person already exists; sent on every 409 of the request.

reasonKey.description: The key of the reason's text in the server's catalogue (locales).

post.summary: A teacher of the course ends one student's membership. The body is exactly {}; removed is false when that user holds no open student membership there.
A teacher of the course lets one removed student enrol again; the student still needs a valid code. The body is exactly {}; allowed is false when nothing was blocking that student there.
One work's exception from the language of its assignment, keyed by the student; {language: null} removes it. At most 128 bytes. Answers the language the work has afterwards.

200.description: the language the work has now

get.summary: The teacher roles of the session's institution, for its administrator: pending (whom a role confirmation would confirm, with the time of an earlier revocation or null) and confirmed (with the time of confirmation and forReview, no current teacher right at the last login, D-200), each by family and given name (hr collation), then id, those without a name last. No time of the last login. No query; any query is 422. Anyone who is not a confirmed administrator is 403.

put.summary: The holder replaces the group's assistant and student lists atomically. Each list has distinct IDs. Assistants must be on the roster and students enrolled in the course. A student with a place in another group causes 409.

get.summary: The people the holder can add as assistants: confirmed teachers of the same institution who are neither a teacher of the course nor an active assistant, ordered by name. Only an ID and a display name, never an address or another identifier. Anyone but the holder is refused.

200.description: the candidates for the assistant roster

get.summary: The teaching team screen. The holder gets the roster, the enrolled students with their group and the groups with their assistants. An assistant gets only the groups where they hold a place, with the students in them. Anyone else is refused.

200.description: the team view for the caller's role

get.summary: The current holder and active assistants, readable by the holder and active assistants.

post.summary: The holder replaces the entire assistant roster with distinct IDs. Omitting an assistant ends all their group places in the course. Adding an assistant alone grants no access to works.

get.summary: The forms of the caller's faculty for a thesis (for example the topic application, the statement of originality as the official name of the form, the statement of deposit): the newest version of each code. Retired forms are listed for the administrator only.

200.description: The forms in force, by code

post.summary: The administrator of the faculty publishes a new version of a form (version 1 for a new code). A version is only ever added; active = false retires the form.

get.summary: The theses of the administrator's faculty for the registrar's office: kind of work, mentor, student, stage after the submission, date of the defence, state of the topic and number of committee members. Read only, in the order of the date of the defence (works with none last), then the id of the mentorship: no ranking and no grade. Query: stage (one of none, submitted_to_office, defense_scheduled, defended), limit (1 to 200, default 50) and after (the next of the previous page, so no page skips or repeats a work). Any other parameter, a repeated one and a value that is none of these are 422. Another faculty's works are never seen. A teacher, a student and anyone else with a session are 403.

200.description: A page of theses, possibly none

get.summary: The faculty's switch for the mentor's consent to a submission (off by default: no row) and when it was last set.

put.summary: The administrator sets the faculty's switch. Setting the value in force writes nothing.

post.summary: A teacher of the assignment sets the language its works are written in, against the version they saw: {expectedVersion, language}, at most 128 bytes, sent as application/json (only the media type before any parameter is judged). A malformed assignment id is 422; a stale version or a work already asked to be submitted is 409 conflict. Answers the new version.

get.summary: The work template of one work type of the caller's institution, for an administrator of it: current is the latest version, or null while there is none, and versions is the whole history in ascending order. Each version is {version, effectiveFrom, titlePage, sections, citationStyle}: titlePage the fields of the title page in order (title, author, mentor, course, date), sections the skeleton {title, hint}, citationStyle fpzg. No query. A work type outside the set is 422 invalid_input. A teacher, a student and an account without a confirmed role are 403.

200.description: the current version and the history

put.summary: An administrator of the institution replaces the work template of one work type with a new version: exactly {expectedVersion, titlePage, sections, citationStyle}, at most 64 KiB, sent as application/json. expectedVersion is the latest version the administrator saw for this work type (0 when none); another version added in between is 409 conflict. titlePage is at most 5 distinct fields out of title, author, mentor, course, date, in the order of the page. sections is at most 30 objects, each exactly {title, hint}: a title of 1 to 120 characters, a hint of 0 to 400 characters, neither with control characters; citationStyle is fpzg; anything else, including an unknown key and a work type outside the set, is 422 invalid_input. Works and assignments that already exist are not changed. A teacher, a student and an account without a confirmed role are 403. The institution and the author come from the session, never from the body.

get.summary: What the page for one work's language shows a teacher: the work's title, the language of its assignment and the work's own exception (null when it follows the assignment). Keyed by the document id so the student's id never reaches the browser. A document that is not a work of this teacher's assignment, another teacher's or another institution's assignment and a missing one all read alike (403); a malformed assignment or document id is 422.

200.description: the work's title, its assignment's language and its exception

post.summary: The same exception keyed by the work's document id, so the student's id never reaches the browser; a document that is not a work of this teacher's assignment is refused like another teacher's (403). A malformed document id is 422, judged after the content type and the body.

200.description: the language the work has now

get.summary: The last published state of a work, the same bytes and ETag for the owner and the teacher. The request carries `ductus-protocol: 1` (and Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin when the browser sends it), else 403; a teacher's read writes the access log. `If-None-Match: "<etag>"` with the ETag last read answers 304. After the submission the bytes are the submitted revision, marked `ductus-live-state: submitted`. 204 when nothing is published yet.

304.description: the state of the ETag sent

put.summary: Publishes the last state of a work (the student owner only). The body is the exact JCS bytes of a valid document snapshot, at most 2 MiB. The request carries exactly one precondition: `If-None-Match: *` for the first write or `If-Match: "<token>"` with the last token, else 428. 200 {outcome, token} when accepted or unchanged; 409 {outcome: "conflict", token} with the current token (null when nothing is published yet) when the token is stale. The session is checked before the first body byte.

200.description: accepted, or the same state again

409.description: the token is stale: the current one, null when nothing is published

get.summary: The effective deadline, dated milestones and consultation slots of one active mentorship, in chronological order. Only its student and mentor may read.

200.description: Dates ordered by instant, kind and id. The deadline id is the assignment id.

get.summary: List the current mentor's private notes for an active mentorship, oldest first.

post.summary: Add a private note as the current mentor of an active mentorship.

The confirmed teacher opens a mentorship of a kind of work for a student of the own institution, with an optional topic (1 to 300 code points, not blank). The mentorship, its work and the first version exist from the commit on, and the student gets one notification (notifications.mentorship-opened.list.get). The student does not ask; an older student request stays as it is. A student who is unknown, of another institution, holds a confirmed teacher role or is the caller, and a caller who is no confirmed teacher, read 404; an open mentorship of the kind is 409; a missing faculty rule for the kind is 503.

get.summary: MK-8: every open mentorship of the caller in one read, newest mentorship first (the order of teacher.mentorships.get; no score, no rank, no comparison of students). Each has the current stage, whom the work waits on (mentor: a submitted stage or a message of the student the caller has not opened; student: the work not opened, or the stage not submitted or under revision; none otherwise), the next deadline of a milestone that is not approved (a revision deadline first) with its days in Europe/Zagreb, and the number of the student's messages the caller has not opened. A caller who mentors nobody reads an empty list.

post.summary: The confirmed teacher the request was made to approves it; the mentorship, its work and the first version exist from the commit on. Approving again answers the same mentorship and writes nothing. Anyone else, the student and another institution's teacher included, and an unknown or malformed id read 404; a declined or withdrawn request is 409; a missing faculty rule for the kind is 503. No body.

200.description: the approved request and its mentorship

post.summary: The confirmed teacher the request was made to declines it. The optional reason (1 to 600 code points, not blank) stays in the audit record; the student is not shown it. Declining again answers the same and writes nothing. Anyone else and an unknown or malformed id read 404; an approved or withdrawn request is 409.

The student withdraws the own open request. Withdrawing again answers the same and writes nothing. Anyone else and an unknown or malformed id read 404; an approved or declined request is 409. No body.

The student asks a confirmed teacher of the own institution to mentor one work of a kind. Creates no mentorship. A teacher who is unknown, of another institution, unconfirmed, revoked or the caller reads 404; an open request or an open mentorship of the kind is 409.

get.summary: The confirmed, unrevoked teachers of the caller's own institution, other than the caller: exactly the teachers mentorship.requests.post accepts. Only the account, the name pair and the department; never an address or another personal datum. Ordered by family name, given name and id. A caller with a confirmed teacher role is 403.

200.description: teachers the caller may ask, possibly none

get.summary: The caller's own open mentorships as their student, newest first: the kind of work, the assignment, the topic of an opening, the mentor and whether the teacher opened it or approved a request. A caller with a confirmed teacher role is 403.

The caller's own mentorship requests in every state, newest first, each with the teacher asked, the kind of work and the instants. The decline reason stays in the audit record (P-6). A caller with a confirmed teacher role is 403.

The signed-in account's inbox, newest first. Start without a cursor; pass nextBefore as before to continue. The first page may materialize a deadline reminder for the caller. A target identifier carries no access to the target.

The signed-in student's notifications that a teacher opened a mentorship for them, newest first, each with the kind of work, the topic and the mentor. Only the student of the mentorship sees one. Start without a cursor; pass nextBefore as before to continue. Mark one read with notifications.read.post. notifications.list.get leaves these out.

post.summary: Marks the caller's own notification as read. A retry preserves the first read time. Unknown and inaccessible identifiers return the same 404.

get.summary: The signed-in student's notifications that a teacher returned a work for revision, newest first, each with the work, the teacher's comment and the new revision due date. Only the student owner of the work sees one. Start without a cursor; pass nextBefore as before to continue. Mark one read with notifications.read.post.

The operator's read of the log: the records of a window, at most 1000 a page, in seq order, each as the operator read (operator_log) masks it (an address only as a network: the host part is always cut, a mask longer than /24 for IPv4 or /48 for IPv6 is cut to it, a shorter one such as /8 stays; a field whose name is not an ASCII letter followed only by ASCII letters and digits, or holds token, cookie, secret, password, credential, bearer, authorization or session in any case, is left out; a value the read cannot vouch for is "hidden"). The pipeline decides who reaches it, before the route: 403 forbidden from a network outside the list (step 3), or for an account not on the operator list of the server or without a confirmed second factor (step 8); 401 unauthenticated without a live session (step 8); 503 unavailable when step 8 cannot ask the operator list or the second factor. from and to are UTC instants of the calendar, the window is from inclusive to exclusive, from before to and at most 24 hours apart (exactly 24 is allowed); after is the seq the page starts after (0 by default), a decimal of 0 to 2^53-1 without a leading zero. A repeated or unknown parameter, or a window outside these bounds, is 422 and reads nothing. next is the seq of the last event when the page is full (1000), to pass as after, and may then lead to an empty page; null when the page is shorter. A row the read cannot vouch for makes the whole answer 503, never a shorter page.

200.description: a page of events, possibly none

get.summary: Whole-server technical numbers of the pilot for an operator (plan P-D6): recorded submissions and requests without one, signed receipts and submissions still without one, help requests and those reporting a save problem, and the median and 95th percentile from a submission request to its signed receipt. Counted up to asOf, the start of the current day in Zagreb. No identifier, no text, no breakdown and no filter. A count from 1 to 4 is null, and so is any count derivable from the published ones by subtraction; a shown count is rounded down to a multiple of five. The durations are null below five receipts and whenever the receipt counts are hidden, and capped at 2147483647 ms.

post.summary: The teacher allocates the round once, with no body. The allocation is deterministic (the seed is the roundId, so the same round and the same submitted works give the same allocation) and only among students whose work is submitted: nobody reviews their own work, no two students review each other's, and everyone reviews and is reviewed exactly reviewsPerStudent times. Fewer submitted works than the round needs (see peer-review.round.get, minSubmissions) is 409 too_few_submissions, and nothing is allocated: with too few works a reviewer could work out the author of the work they read. A second allocation is 409 already_allocated; a round that does not exist reads 404. The answer is the number of allocations made.

The teacher of the assignment withdraws a submitted review with a reason of 1 to 600 code points. The review is not deleted: it stays for the teacher and disappears from the answer of student.peer-reviews-received.get. A withdrawal is never undone; a review that is already withdrawn is 409 conflict, one that is still pending (not written) reads 404. Another's, an unknown and a malformed review all read 404.

get.summary: The round of the assignment for its teacher, or null with state none. state is none, not_allocated, allocated (before opensAt), open or closed (after dueAt). submittedWorks counts the works of the assignment that are submitted and minSubmissions is the fewest a round needs to be allocated (never fewer than 5, and 2 * reviewsPerStudent + 1): it is there so the teacher sees why an allocation is refused, not to compare students. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment reads 404.

put.summary: The teacher of the assignment sets its round of peer review: opensAt before dueAt, reviewsPerStudent 1 to 3 and 1 to 6 rubrics, each a key (a short lowercase word, unique in the round) and a one-line label of 1 to 120 code points. There is at most one round per assignment; setting it again replaces it only while it is not allocated, after that it is 409 already_allocated. opensAt not before dueAt and repeated keys are 422 invalid_input. No rubric is a grade or carries points. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment reads 404.

get.summary: The allocations of the round for its teacher, who sees both ends: reviewer and author by name. Ordered by reviewer's family name, given name, id, then author's the same way. reviewId is null while the review is pending and carries the id the withdrawal route takes otherwise. It is a list of facts: no score, no count per student, no order by quality. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment reads 404; an assignment with no allocated round has no allocations.
Liveness: the process answers. Reads no database, session or environment.

200.description: alive. Since 1.3.0 also the state of the main database (`state`, checked with a time limit) and the versions; never an address, a name or an error.

state.description: degraded: the main database is not ok or did not answer in time

minClientVersion.description: oldest client version this server serves

get.summary: Readiness per capability, closed words only.
Public status in three parts, closed words, nothing about a person.

maintenanceWindows.description: Current and upcoming planned maintenance, ordered by start time. Omitted when the schedule could not be read.

get.summary: The entries of a placement, oldest date first, then createdAt, then entryId, with the signoffs (latest first). Read by the student of the placement and its mentor, and by no one else; another's, an unknown or a malformed placement reads 404. A corrected entry stays listed; the entry that corrects it names it.

post.summary: The student of the placement adds an entry: date (not in the future, inside the period), hours (0.5 to 12 in steps of 0.5), text (1 to 4000 code points) and, to correct an earlier entry of the same placement, correctsEntryId. Entries are only added: nothing is changed or removed, a signed entry stays as signed and a correction after a signoff needs a new signoff. A date outside the period is 409 placement_closed; the 401st entry is 409 conflict. The mentor and anyone else read 404.

get.summary: The placements of the caller: a student reads their own, a teacher only those of mentorships they are the mentor of. Latest start first, then placementId. entryCount counts every entry, corrections included; signedThrough is the latest throughDate of a signoff (not a promise that every later-added entry up to it is signed), null while none exists. It is a list of facts: no hours total, no comparison, no state of good or bad.

post.summary: The mentor of an active mentorship opens a placement for its student: the organisation (one line, 1 to 120 code points) and the period (startsOn on or before endsOn). A mentorship id that is not a UUID is 422 invalid_input; one that is another's, unknown or ended reads 404. A student has no such call. The placement belongs to that mentorship and has that one mentor.

get.summary: The signoffs of a placement, latest first, then signoffId. The same answer for the student of the placement and its mentor; the mentor's private notes are never part of it. Another's, an unknown or a malformed placement reads 404.

post.summary: The mentor signs every entry of the placement up to and including throughDate that exists now: the answer says how many and the JCS SHA-256 of that set. A signoff is a record in Ductura of who signed which set and when, with an optional comment (up to 1000 code points); it is not a qualified signature and is never withdrawn (a later signoff replaces it in the view, the earlier one stays in the history). throughDate must not be in the future and must lie inside the period of the placement, else 422 invalid_input; so signedThrough only ever names a date that was in the past and in the period when it was signed. Entries added later for a date up to it are corrections that need a new signoff: signedThrough does not say that every entry up to that date is signed, entryCount and entriesSha256 of the signoff say which were. With no entry to sign it is 409 nothing_to_sign. The student and anyone else read 404.

get.summary: The caller's saved interface language, or null.

post.summary: Saves the caller's interface language. Canonical JSON, nothing but the locale.

get.summary: The caller's institution, roles in force and display name.

delete.summary: Starting over as profile.self-note-key.delete, but only under the key the device names: deletes the caller's note key and, in the same transaction, every sealed note of the caller, only when keyId is the key the caller keeps now and, when the query names ifVersion, only at that version. No key, another keyId or another version is 409 and changes nothing, so a device that read the key before another device rewrapped it or started over deletes nothing it has not seen. A keyId that is not a lowercase UUID, an ifVersion that is not a decimal 1 to 999999999 or any other query parameter is 422. Answers {key: null}.

Starting over after the phrase and the recovery code are both lost: deletes the caller's note key and, in the same transaction, every sealed note of the caller on every work; the reading places stay. Nobody, the institution included, can restore them. Deleting no key changes nothing. Answers {key: null}.

get.summary: The caller's own note key, wrapped by the phrase and by the recovery code (B2), with its version; null until it is set. Nobody reads another person's key. The server never sees the text, the place of the note, the phrase, the recovery code or the note key.

put.summary: Sets the caller's note key ({v: 1, keyId, kdf, phrase, recovery, ifVersion: null}, only when none is kept) or rewraps the same key under a new phrase or recovery code (ifVersion the current version, the same keyId); the version then rises by one. Any other case (a key already there, none there, another keyId, another version) is 409 and changes nothing, so two devices never overwrite each other. kdf PBKDF2-SHA-256 with 600000 to 10000000 iterations; each wrap has its own 16-byte salt, a 12-byte iv and 48 bytes of wrapped key, in base64url. The server never sees the text, the place of the note, the phrase, the recovery code or the note key.

get.summary: The caller's own staff affiliation: its source and when a login last confirmed it, or the closed code staff_affiliation_missing. Without one the person stays a student and no teacher role can be confirmed; another institution's affiliation is never recorded.

200.description: the affiliation, or the closed code without one

post.summary: The same accepted record for the owner and course teacher, with active editing minutes (sum of session spans excluding record gaps) and the coarse times of recorded imports and assistant transfers.

The process summary of one work, built from the accepted evidence only, as its JCS bytes. The body is exactly {documentId}, at most 1 KiB; any other key is 422. A work the caller may not read, or that does not exist, is 404; a record that does not verify is 503, never a partial summary.

Checks whether a signed submission receipt binds exactly the given text (C-6). The body is the two values of the receipt's QR fragment: the submission id and the SHA-256 of the submitted text, lowercase. Works without a login, never reads or sets a session cookie and is not a way to sign in (D-09); it has its own rate limit per address. match is true only when the institution's receipt for that submission names that hash and its Ed25519 signature verifies with a key valid then and not revoked; the answer then carries only the submission and signing instants and the key id, never a name, course, assignment or text. Every other case, an unknown submission included, is the same match false.

get.summary: The settings catalogue: every key, the levels that may hold it, its kind, default and hard limits.

The rows of one level in the caller's scope (course names the course for the course level and is absent for every other), and for every catalogue key of that level the value that holds without it (source: a higher level or default) and the narrowest higher bound. A level or course that is not the caller's gives 404, the same as a course that does not exist (C-23: another's is nonexistent).

200.description: the level's rows and what it inherits

put.summary: Sets the caller's value and bound of one key at one level (the bound as locked, min and max); no value and no bound remove the row and the level above holds again. course is a course id for the course level and null for every other. A level or course that is not the caller's gives 404, the same as a course that does not exist. A key outside the catalogue, a level the catalogue does not allow for it, a value of the wrong kind or out of its limits and a bound of a wrong shape give 422; crossing a higher bound gives 409. A refusal of the catalogue (422) comes before the level check (404), as in settings.set_value. 409 needs a key a lower level holds under a higher bound; the first catalogue has none, so its vector shows the shape only. Every change is kept with its author, time, old and new value.

200.description: saved (changed is false when the row already held it)

post.summary: Find bibliographic metadata for one DOI or ISBN in a catalogue, for synthetic students in local development.

200.description: Metadata for the source, or null when the catalogue has no record.

post.summary: Starts the caller's own work on an assignment of their open student membership, or answers the one already started: at most one work per student and assignment, so a second start answers the same workId and writes nothing. Answers the work id, the version of the institution's rules the assignment is pinned to (null for an assignment made before any) and the language of the work. No body. Another course's assignment, an unknown one and a malformed id are the same 404 (C-23); a notice not yet acknowledged or an assignment not yet open is 409 conflict and nothing is written; an institution without one evidence domain is 503.

200.description: the caller's work, started now or before

get.summary: The caller's own started works on the assignments of their open student memberships, by due time, then assignment id: the assignment and course as the student sees them, the caller's due time, state, revision, submission time and work language. Nothing of a teacher (grade, note, accommodation, criteria) and no other person. A caller with no work gets an empty list.

Who opened the caller's own work and when (PRODUCT §5 rule 17): one entry per stored opening of five minutes, newest first; the client groups them into Europe/Zagreb days. No total of visits and no duration (D-274 MQ10). The query names the oldest entry shown, beforeAt and beforeId from next; a page from it holds only windows strictly older. Only both together, on the five-minute grid, a lowercase UUID, not in the future and not before year one are a cursor; anything else, and any other parameter, reads the first page with continued false, never an error, so every opening stays reachable. Another's work, an unknown and a malformed id read the same 404 (C-23). A row the read cannot vouch for makes the whole answer 503.

200.description: a page of openings, possibly none

get.summary: How many assistant requests a student of the assignment may send today and has sent, as {limit, used}: limit is the daily number of requests per student and assignment the institution set, null when it set none; used counts today's requests (Europe/Zagreb) that were not refused. A number of requests, never an amount. Over the limit the request route answers budget_exceeded. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.

Whether the assistant is available for the assignment, for a student of its course: true exactly when the server has a provider, the institution has a published cost configuration and the course did not switch the assistant off. The assignment's own rules still decide what the assistant may do. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.

The code tests of an assignment the caller is enrolled in, to run in their own browser: {revisionNo, language, tests}, a test being {id, title, input, expected} (input and expected any JSON value). revisionNo 0, language javascript and no tests while none is set. A teacher and a student of the assignment read the same latest revision on either path (the tests are visible to the student); a teacher of another course, another institution, a mentored assignment, an unknown and a malformed assignment id all read the same 404. No result of a run is ever sent or stored.

The format rules the work on this assignment is checked against before submission: {wordMin, wordMax, minSources, requiredSections, citationStyle, font, size, spacing}. wordMin and wordMax are the word range of the current assignment version (null leaves that end open); requiredSections are the section titles of the template frozen on the assignment, in order, and empty when it uses none; citationStyle is the style of the template, fpzg without one; minSources is 0 because the assignment sets no minimum; font, size and spacing are null until the rules package is available. No query. The check built on these rules is advisory and never blocks a submission. An assignment of a course the caller is not a student of, a mentorship assignment, an unknown and a malformed id are the same 404 (C-23).
Whether a submission after the deadline of the assignment is allowed, for a student of its course. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.

The word range of the current assignment version. A null bound leaves that end open; when both bounds are present min is at most max. A null range means neither bound is set. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.

The rubric of an assignment the caller is enrolled in, before submitting: {version, criteria}. While the teacher set none the answer is version 0 and the six default criteria of the working criteria (topic, structure, sources, method, language, formatting), each with three levels; only in this version 0 are the titles and level labels message keys (workingCriteria.<id>, assignmentRubric.levelLow, levelMid, levelHigh) for the client to show, a stored rubric carries the teacher's own words. No mark, level chosen, number, sum or grade of any work is in it. A teacher, a student of another course, another institution, an unknown and a malformed assignment id all read the same 404.

200.description: the rubric, or the default criteria

get.summary: When the caller's own submission was confirmed, for every assignment student.assignment-work.get would list at the same instant: one row per assignment, by assignmentId (lowercase). With a signed receipt, submittedAt and afterDeadline are receipt.payload.requestedAt and receipt.payload.afterDeadline of the receipt student.submission.get returns. With no submission, a withdrawn one or one still waiting for its receipt (ceka), both are null. The identity comes from the session only, so the list holds only the caller's own assignments. A row or a receipt the read cannot vouch for makes the whole answer 503, never a partial list.

200.description: ready (an empty list when the student has no course)

get.summary: A student of the assignment's course reads the work template frozen on the assignment: {version, titlePage, sections, citationStyle}, titlePage the fields of the title page in order, sections the skeleton {title, hint}. No query. An assignment that uses no template, an assignment of a course the caller is not a student of, a mentorship assignment, an unknown and a malformed id are the same 404 (C-23).

The state of the caller's own work for every assignment student.assignments.get would list at the same instant: one row per assignment, by assignmentId (lowercase). submitted: the caller has a recorded submission for the assignment, of any of its versions; in_progress: the caller has a work for it (one per student and assignment) and no recorded submission; not_started: no work. The two reads are separate, so a client joins them by lowercase id and shows no state for an assignment without a row on both sides. The identity comes from the session only. A row the read cannot vouch for makes the whole answer 503, never a partial list.

200.description: ready (an empty list when the student has no course and no open mentorship with an assignment); the rows also cover every assignment student.mentored-assignments.get would list

lateException.description: The caller's own latest late-submission exception on the assignment: the teacher's record that this student may still submit until untilAt although the deadline has passed, even when late submission is not allowed (a submission then is still after the deadline). Absent when the caller has none; sent also after untilAt, so a client compares untilAt with the time. Another student's exception is never in the answer.

get.summary: The courses of the caller's open student memberships and the current version of every assignment in each. Courses by name (hr collation), then id; assignments by due time, then id. The identity comes from the session only.

200.description: ready (an empty list when the student has no course)

get.summary: The student's own AI assistant conversation, messages by seq, each with the state of its request: a paragraph stays when its request ended without a response. Nobody else reads it, the teacher included. A foreign, unknown or malformed conversation id returns 404.

The caller's own AI assistant conversations of an assignment of which they are a student (of its course or its mentorship), newest activity first, then id: no message text, which student.assistant-conversation.get reads. Nobody else's conversation is ever listed, the teacher's view included. The identity comes from the session only. Sec-Fetch-Site, when sent, other than same-origin is 403. Another's assignment, an unknown one and a malformed id are the same 404 (C-23); an assignment without a conversation is an empty list. A row the read cannot vouch for makes the whole answer 503.

200.description: the conversations (an empty list when there is none)

post.summary: A student of the assignment asks the AI assistant about one paragraph for one purpose. The Idempotency-Key header holds a UUID per account: the same key with the same request answers what is already there and never calls the provider again; with another request it answers idempotency_conflict. The provider and the model come from the server's versioned configuration and are never taken from the request; after a provider failure no other provider is tried. 200 always carries outcome from the closed set: completed with the response, or idempotency_conflict, forbidden (a foreign and an unknown assignment or conversation alike), ai_disabled, purpose_not_allowed, budget_exceeded, in_progress, request_outcome_unknown or provider_failed. A body outside the contract is 422 invalid_input (outcome invalid_request of the contract); a missing, repeated or malformed key is 428 precondition_required (outcome invalid_idempotency_key). Neither leaves a row, so the key stays free.

get.summary: The required literature of a course the caller is a student of, oldest first then by id. A course the caller is not a student of, an unknown and a malformed id answer 404.

Download of a ready student data export through its one-time link, without a session (a former student may have none): application/zip (izvoz-mojih-podataka.zip) the first time within 24 hours of the package being ready, as an attachment; the same contents give the same bytes and X-Content-SHA256 is the SHA-256 of the body. The ZIP holds manifest.json, the submitted texts and receipt PDFs under predaje/, biljeske.json and dnevnik-pristupa.json. A used, expired or unknown link is 410, as a problem.

200.description: ZIP bytes; the contract format has no binary body

get.summary: The caller's individual and assignment-wide extensions, oldest first. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.

post.summary: Send raw PDF or UTF-8 plain-text bytes with Content-Type application/pdf or text/plain. Other media types yield 415; bytes that do not match the type yield 422. Uploading returns a reference for a later declaration PUT.

get.summary: Read the student's declaration, the current faculty form when configured, and the metadata of external uploads.

text.description: Up to 2000 Unicode code points, NFC, no leading or trailing space, no control character but the line feed.

put.summary: Save a draft or confirm an immutable declaration for the current document revision. A stale base, unconfirmed fields, an outdated form or a submission request returns 409.

humanHelp.description: Closed declaration-v1 object with received and entries [{kind,text}].

ai.description: Closed declaration-v1 object with use, declaredTools, empty attachments, and externalAttachmentIds.

text.description: Up to 2000 Unicode code points, NFC, no leading or trailing space, no control character but the line feed.
Up to 2000 Unicode code points, NFC, no leading or trailing space, no control character but the line feed.

409.description: conflict, already_submitted, form_outdated, incomplete, declaration_conflict, stale_revision, mandatory_attachment_missing, attachment_stale

post.summary: Enrols the caller in the course of a code. The body is exactly {code}, at most 64 UTF-16 units and 1 KiB, sent as application/json (charset utf-8 only). The server normalizes the code (white space and hyphens removed, upper case); what is left must be 8 to 32 letters and digits, else it is invalid_code. outcome: enrolled; already_enrolled, the caller is a student of that course already and nothing changed; enrolled_no_assignment, enrolled in a course without an assignment yet. A code no course of the caller's institution has is 422 invalid_code; a code whose validity has ended is 422 expired_code. Too many guesses are 429 too_many_attempts, and each invalid or expired guess counts. The identity comes from the session only.

200.description: enrolled, already enrolled, or enrolled in a course without an assignment

get.summary: The caller's own late-submission exceptions, oldest first; each carries kind exception, the mark the student sees. Nothing of another student. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.

The current version of every assignment of the caller's open mentorships whose mentor holds a confirmed teacher role: the works the caller may open by the mentorship relation, not by a course. By due time, then id. The identity comes from the session only. A row the read cannot vouch for makes the whole answer 503, never a partial list.

200.description: ready (an empty list when the student has no open mentorship with an assignment)

post.summary: Records that the caller read the notice of the given version of an assignment of their open student membership (PO-7). The body is exactly {versionNo}, at most 128 bytes, sent as application/json (charset utf-8 only). Idempotent: a repeated call answers the first readAt. A malformed assignment id is 400 invalid_assignment_id, judged before the session; another's assignment and an unknown one are the same 404 (C-23); a version that is no longer current is 409 conflict and nothing is recorded.

get.summary: The notice of the current version of an assignment of the caller's open student membership (E-6): the content of that version as the notice shows it, the notice template version, and when the caller first read it (PO-7, student.notice-read.post) and acknowledged it (institution.acknowledgment.post), each null until then. The fields are exactly those of the notice fingerprint (DAN-306), instants as Date.toISOString writes them; the browser computes the fingerprint from them and sends it with versionNo to institution.acknowledgment.post. aiPurposes is empty when aiPolicy is prohibited. The identity comes from the session only. Sec-Fetch-Site, when sent, other than same-origin is 403. Another's assignment, an unknown one and a malformed id are the same 404 (C-23). A row the read cannot vouch for makes the whole answer 503.

The reviews the student is to write in the round of an assignment of their course. state is disabled (the faculty has the review off), none (no round, or this student has no allocation: a work that was not submitted is not allocated), open (between opensAt and dueAt) or closed (after dueAt). A task is only its taskId, whether it is pending or submitted, and the deadline: nothing about the work or its author. The tasks of a round that is not yet open are not listed. It is not a count to compare, and a student who has written nothing has no mark. Another's, an unknown and a malformed assignment read 404.

The submitted work the task is for, as its allocated reviewer reads it, and the rubrics to review it by. Anonymous: the answer has no field of any person, of the work, of the assignment or of the course, and the document is only the text of the submitted revision as blocks of a kind and a text: the title page, the signature and the metadata of the blocks (authors, timestamps, ids, marks) are not part of it. It is read only while the round is open and only by the student the task is allocated to; before opening, after the deadline, or by anyone else (the author included) it reads 404, the same as an unknown or malformed task. A text the author wrote about themselves in the body of the work is the author's own and is not looked for.

200.description: the rubrics and the anonymised work

post.summary: The allocated reviewer writes the review of the task's work: one text of 1 to 4000 code points for each rubric of the round (exactly those keys, once each, else 422 invalid_input) and an optional general comment of up to 4000 code points. It is written once and only added: it cannot be changed or removed by the student. After the deadline it is 409 closed; a second one for the same task is 409 already_reviewed. A task that is not the caller's, an unknown or a malformed one reads 404, as does one of a round that is not yet open. There is no score and no rating.

get.summary: The reviews of the caller's own work in the round, oldest first, then reviewId. Anonymous: no field of the reviewer, of the allocation or of the task, and a withdrawn review is not listed (the teacher keeps it). Each item carries the rubrics it answers by key and label (as the round had them) and the optional general comment. Nothing is summed, scored or ranked. Without a round, or with no review yet, the list is empty; another's, an unknown and a malformed assignment read 404.

Download the portable record of the caller's own submission as application/zip (prenosivi-zapis.zip). The ZIP holds manifest.json (format ductura.portable-record.v1: the submission id, dailyRoot included or pending, and every other file with its size and SHA-256), potvrda.json (the signed submission receipt V2), kljuc-potvrde.json (its public key and validity), rad.json (the exact submitted text, whose SHA-256 is the receipt's artifactSha256), potvrda-predaje.pdf (the receipt PDF; its QR carries only the submission id and that SHA-256, in the URL fragment) and, once the day of signing is closed, dnevni-korijen.json, kljuc-dnevnog-korijena.pem and merkle-dokaz.json (the signed daily root and the inclusion proof of the receipt's entry). The same submission gives the same bytes; X-Content-SHA256 is the SHA-256 of the ZIP. Another's, an unknown or a malformed submission, and one without a signed receipt, return 404.

200.description: ZIP bytes (application/zip); the contract format has no binary body

delete.summary: Deletes a code of the caller's codebook; the others close up. A code with marked passages is deleted together with them only when the query says confirm=true; without it that is 409 conflict and nothing is removed. A code without passages needs no confirmation. Another's, an unknown and a malformed code read 404.

patch.summary: Renames, re-describes or moves a code of the caller's codebook: any of name, description and order (the place, 1 = first; the others keep their order), at least one. A place outside 1 to the number of codes is 422 invalid_input; a name another code has, the case aside, is 409 conflict. Another's, an unknown and a malformed code read 404. The answer is the code as it now is.

get.summary: The caller's own codebook for qualitative coding, in its own order (order 1 first), never by use. Possibly empty. Only the owner reads it: a teacher, a mentor and another student see nothing of it.

200.description: the codebook, in the owner's order

post.summary: Adds a code to the end of the caller's codebook: name (one line, 1 to 80 code points) and an optional description (one line, up to 500; none is empty).
