A name the codebook already has, the case aside, and the 201st code are 409 conflict. The answer is the code with its place. Nothing here proposes a code.

get.summary: The caller's coding as qualitative-export-v1: the codebook (code, name, description) in its own order, the marked passages (material, code, place, quote, memo) in the order of the codebook, then of the materials in the order they were kept in, then of the text, and the count of passages per code and material in the same order. Never ordered by the count, with no 'most often' and no comparison of materials (V18-8). With the query materialId only that material's passages (and counts) are listed; a material that is not the caller's, an unknown and a malformed materialId are the same 404; any other query, or materialId twice, is 422 invalid_input. The same coding gives the same bytes. Only the owner reads it; it is a description to be carried away, not a verdict.

delete.summary: Deletes one of the caller's own materials together with its marked passages. A material of someone else, an unknown id and a malformed id are the same 404.

get.summary: Reads one of the caller's own materials with its text, the number of marked passages (segmentCount) and whether it is locked. A material of someone else, an unknown id and a malformed id are the same 404.

Lists the caller's own materials for qualitative coding, newest first and without the text: title, kind (interview or note), the day it was kept, its length in characters, the number of marked passages and whether it is locked (it has a marked passage). Nobody else's material is ever listed. No route of this family calls the assistant.

post.summary: Keeps a typed or pasted text as the caller's own material: exactly {title, kind, text}. The title is one line of 1..200 characters, kind is interview or note, the text is 1..100 000 characters with something visible and no control character but a line break and a tab (a pasted \r\n is kept as \n). There is no sound and no automatic transcript. A person keeps up to 200 materials (409 conflict beyond that). A text cannot be changed after it is kept: a change is a new material. Answers 201 with the material. A body that is not exactly this is 422.

delete.summary: Removes one marked passage of the caller. A passage of someone else, an unknown id and a malformed id are the same 404.

get.summary: Reads the passages the caller has marked in one of their own materials, in the order of the text (paragraph, start, end): code, place, quote, memo (null when there is none) and the day it was marked. A material of someone else, an unknown id and a malformed id are the same 404.

post.summary: Marks a passage of one of the caller's own materials with one of the caller's own codes: exactly {codeId, anchor{paragraph, start, end, quote}, memo?}. The anchor is characters start..end (0-based, end exclusive, counted in characters) of line number paragraph of the text, and the quote must be exactly those characters, 1..500 of them and not only blank (422 invalid_input otherwise). The memo is 1..1000 characters, or left out. A material or a code that is not the caller's, an unknown one and a malformed id are the same 404. The same mark again (same code and place) and the 5001st passage of a material are 409 conflict. Marking locks the material: its text cannot change anyway. Answers 201 with the passage. Nothing marks or suggests a code by itself.

A student of the course answers an open questionnaire once: exactly {answers[{questionId, value}]}, one answer per question at most, at least one, each of the kind of its question (single: an option code; multiple: distinct option codes; scale: an integer in the scale; number: a finite number; text: a line of text). The sheet is stored without the person; only the fact of taking part is kept. A second answer is 409 conflict and stores nothing. A body that is not exactly this, an answer that does not fit its question and a question that is not of this questionnaire are 422. A draft, a closed, another course's, an unknown or a malformed questionnaire id returns 404.

get.summary: The form of an open questionnaire of a course the student is enrolled in, questions in the author's order. A draft, a closed, another course's, an unknown or a malformed questionnaire id returns the same 404.

The open questionnaires of the courses the student is enrolled in, as {id, courseId, title, participated}: participated is true when this student already answered. A draft, a closed questionnaire and one of a course the student is not in are not listed.
Download the caller's signed submission receipt as a PDF. No signed receipt, an inaccessible assignment or a malformed id returns 404.

200.description: PDF bytes encoded in standard Base64, with a download filename

get.summary: The JPEG bytes of one proof of a source of the caller's own work. The proof is named by its work, source and id together; another student's work, another source or an unknown or malformed id return 404.

200.description: the JPEG bytes of the excerpt

get.summary: The requests for a proof of a source of the caller's own work, oldest first (open and closed). The student answers a request by attaching a proof to the source (student.source-proofs.post). Another student's work, an unknown and a malformed assignment id answer 404.
The proofs (attached excerpts) of one source of the caller's own work, oldest first, then by id. Another student's work, a source that is not in the work, an unknown or a malformed id return 404.

post.summary: Attaches an excerpt to a source of the caller's own work: a multipart form with the JPEG image (at most 1 MiB), the page and an optional note. Only an excerpt is kept: a whole PDF or any other file that is not a JPEG returns 422, as does a work at its bound (200 proofs or 100 MiB). Another student's work or a source that is not in the work returns 404.

get.summary: The caller's submissions and withdrawals of the assignment, oldest first, each with its signed receipt (null while not bound), and whether withdrawal is allowed with the deadline in force. A withdrawal is possible when withdrawalAllowed is true, the deadline has not passed and the last event is a confirmed submission. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.
The caller's notes for an accessible assignment, oldest first, then by id.

post.summary: Adds a note for the caller's assignment. The text has 1 to 600 Unicode code points and contains a non-whitespace character. Notes are append-only and stay separate from the submission and signed receipt.

Ask for a link to the export package (kind package) or to the confirmation for the registrar (kind referada) of the caller's own submission. The answer is the download path with the link token and its expiry, 24 hours after the request; asking again issues a new link and changes nothing stored. Another's, an unknown or a malformed submission returns 404.

get.summary: Download through a link from student.submission-package-link.post, within its 24 hours and with the session that asked for it. Kind package is application/zip (prenosivi-zapis.zip, the portable record: manifest.json is the single D-173 manifest); kind referada is application/pdf (the receipt PDF without the text of the work, as an attachment). The same submission gives the same bytes; X-Content-SHA256 is the SHA-256 of the body. A link of another submission, kind or session is 404, an expired link 410, a cross-site read 403.

200.description: ZIP or PDF bytes; the contract format has no binary body

get.summary: Whether the caller may withdraw the own submission of the assignment now, and the signed withdrawals so far (WEB-1903). withdrawable is the server's decision: the teacher has not switched withdrawal off, the deadline in force has not passed and the last event is a confirmed submission whose receipt is bound; the client never compares a time with a deadline. receipts lists the bound withdrawal receipts, oldest first (the full receipts are in student.submission-history.get). An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.

200.description: the state, with no receipts before a first withdrawal

post.summary: The student withdraws the own confirmed submission of the assignment and gets the signed receipt of the withdrawal; nothing is deleted, and the work can be submitted again (submission.submit.post). No body. A retry returns the same withdrawal. 409 not_allowed: the teacher switched withdrawal off; 409 refused: the deadline in force has passed (an extension counts); 409 not_started: no recorded submission to withdraw; 409 conflict: the submission's receipt is not bound yet or a newer submission is in progress. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404. 503 when the receipt cannot be signed; a retry signs the same frozen receipt.

get.summary: The caller's submission for this assignment. An accessible assignment with no submission returns none. ceka means the submission was recorded but no signed receipt is attached yet. potvrdeno carries the same signed receipt as submission.submit.post. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.

The text checks the caller's institution turns on (enabledCheckIds, in the order of the prototype) and its Lekta profile (lektaProfileId, null when the institution has set none). The answer holds no content of any work. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.

citationStyle.description: The citation style of the caller's institution (catalogue key citation.style); fpzg when the institution has set none. Always sent.

delete.summary: Removes a source the caller added. A source that is not there, a teacher's source (with a requirement) and an inaccessible work all answer 404.

put.summary: Adds the caller's source or changes one the caller added; the source id is chosen by the client and must equal record.id. A work holds at most 500 sources. A source with a requirement is a teacher's: it is not changed here and answers 404, as does an inaccessible work.

get.summary: The sources of the caller's work on an accessible assignment, oldest first, then by id: the ones the caller added and the ones a teacher recommended or required (requirement). An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.

The contribution of the student's own team, by state: disabled, none (no team), pending (a member's part is not yet computed), failed (a computation failed; never with a reason) or ready. ready lists every member in alphabetical order of family name, then given name, with the code points per kind of origin in the fixed order and their total, and the permanent notice not_authorship_evidence. There is no share, rank, comparison, average, threshold or colour. The same bytes as teacher.work-team-contribution.get for the same team. Another's, an unknown or a malformed assignment reads 404.

200.description: the contribution state of the student's team

get.summary: The student's own team on the assignment, by state: disabled (the assignment has no teams), none (not in a team yet; with how the teams are formed and, when the students choose, the open teams as an id and a count of members, never names) or member (the team id and the given and family names of its members in alphabetical order). A student sees only their own team and never another one; an assignment the student is not enrolled in, unknown or malformed reads 404.

post.summary: The student creates a team and becomes its first member (create), joins an open team by teamId (join) or leaves their team (leave); the answer is the state afterwards, as student.work-team.get gives it. create and join are allowed only when the students form the teams; leave is allowed in either formation (a team the teacher formed can be left, and only the teacher adds the student again). teamId is required for join and refused for create and leave. 409 conflict: a team above maxSize, a second team on the same assignment, create or join while the teacher forms the teams or while teams are off, leave without a team, and leave after the student's own part was submitted. A team that is another's, unknown or still empty reads 404 (a student sees an open team only with a member in it). A malformed assignment id in the path is 404; a malformed teamId or action in the body is 422 invalid_input. Teams are never deleted.

200.description: the student's team state after the action

get.summary: The working criteria of the caller's own work, one entry per teacher who set at least one, never merged: the teacher's id and name pair (null when the institution holds none), then the six criteria in the same order and shape as teacher.working-criteria.get, with a null assessment and note where that teacher set nothing. Teachers by family name, then given name, then id; while no teacher has set one the list is empty. Only the student who owns the work; a teacher, another student, an unknown work and a malformed id all read the same 404. The read writes nothing in the access log.

post.summary: The second major of submission.submit.post: the same body, guards, answers and receipt, and one more answer. While the assignment requires a declaration (declarationRequired in student.declaration.get) and none is confirmed for the submitted revision, the submission is refused with 409 declaration_required and nothing is written; the student confirms the declaration and submits again. A retry alone never changes it, so it has no `retry-after`. submission.submit.post answers the same case with 503 request.

409.description: blocked, stale_revision, already_requested, not_acknowledged, not_open, declaration_required

post.summary: The student submits the revision they saw: exactly {documentId, revision}, at most 1 KiB; no time, text of the work or hash comes from the client. Same Origin, `ductus-protocol: 1`. The database clock at the click is the time; the revision is reconstructed and, only when it matches, the submission is recorded and its signed receipt returned. The first click binds: another revision later is 409 already_requested. Another student's or a missing work is 404. 503 carries the stage and `retry-after: 5`.

Marks a report that reaches the caller received or resolved: exactly {status}, at most 256 bytes, sent as application/json. The same state again changes nothing. Every change is kept with the role of who made it. An account that reads no reports is 403; a report that does not reach the caller (another kind, course or institution, or none) is 404; a malformed reference or state is 422.

200.description: the current state of the report

post.summary: Sends a problem report: the user's description and a closed technical context. The body is the JCS form of the value, at most 8 KiB; the description is 1 to 1000 code points, no lone surrogate, with a visible character and no control or bidi character other than newline and tab (checked by the server, answered 422). The route is a page template; the server checks it against its closed list of 27 templates and answers 422 otherwise. At most five reports per account in an hour.

201.description: recorded; the reference the user quotes

get.summary: The problem reports that reach the caller, newest first, at most 500 (truncated says more exist): technical reports for a network engineer of the institution, account reports and course reports naming no course for a confirmed administrator, reports about a course for its teaching team. Each carries what the reporter wrote, the closed technical context and the state, never who sent it. An account that is none of these is 403.

post.summary: Submit a problem report with up to 2000 Unicode code points and receive a reference. The limit is five reports per account in a sliding hour, shared with the support route.

201.description: recorded; the reference the user quotes

get.summary: Whether the caller may see the teacher pages: a confirmed and unrevoked institution role (institution.actor_has_role('teacher')), never the login claims. The session and the role come from one snapshot, so denied is always an open session without the role and allowed always comes with a signed-in principal. scope is principalScope, for the shell of the teacher pages only; it is not the general source of the principal. No session is 401, a database that cannot be asked 503. Names no course, assignment or count: the role alone gives no access to a work (C-23).

The latest code tests of an assignment for the form of its teacher: {revisionNo, language, tests}, a test being {id, title, input, expected} (input and expected any JSON value). revisionNo 0, language javascript and no tests while none is set. A teacher and a student of the assignment read the same latest revision on either path (the tests are visible to the student); a teacher of another course, another institution, a mentored assignment, an unknown and a malformed assignment id all read the same 404.

put.summary: A teacher of the assignment adds the next revision of its code tests: exactly {language, tests}, at most 16 KiB, sent as application/json. language is javascript; tests are 0 to 10, each exactly {id, title, input, expected}: an id of 1 to 32 characters of a-z, 0-9, _ and -, unique in the list; a title of 1 to 120 characters; input and expected any JSON value. More than 10 tests, a repeated id and tests the database finds larger than 16 KiB are 422 invalid_code_tests; any other shape is 422 invalid_input. A stored revision is never changed. The answer is the new {revisionNo, language, tests}. A student of the assignment is 403 forbidden; a teacher of another course, another institution, a mentored and an unknown assignment are the same 404. The institution and the author come from the session, never from the body.

post.summary: A teacher of the assignment's course copies it into a course they also teach: {requestKey, courseId} and optionally new opensAt and dueAt (Date.toISOString), at most 4 KiB. The copy is a new assignment (version 1) with the content of the source's current version; the source is unchanged, and no submission, work or other row about a student is copied. The same key with the same source content and dates answers the same id; otherwise it is 409. An assignment or target course the caller does not teach, a mentorship assignment, an unknown and a malformed id are the same 404 (C-23). An opening not before the deadline, or an AI rule wider than the target course allows, is 422. Success follows the database commit.

get.summary: For each student of the assignment's overview: when the notice was first read and when its latest acknowledged version was acknowledged (UTC minutes), and the revision request with the latest change among the student's works (its state and the five-minute window of that change), with the number of open requests. There is no deadline of a revision. This read opens no work and returns no text of a request. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns the same empty list as an assignment with no students.
Checks whether the assignment is eligible for grading. Practice assignments return 409. Only a teacher of the assignment can read the result.

Submission overview for each student visible to the caller, with a UTC minute and the record state from the signed receipt. A recorded submission awaiting its receipt has a null evidenceRecord. This read opens no work and returns no work text, hash or submission id. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns the same empty list as an assignment with no students.

The latest rubric of an assignment for a teacher of it: {version, criteria}, a criterion being {id, title, levels}, levels exactly three {label, descriptor} from the lowest to the highest. version 0 and no criteria while none is set (the form starts empty; the six default criteria are only what a student reads). Only a teacher of the assignment reads it: a student, a teacher of another course, another institution, an unknown and a malformed assignment id all read the same 404.

put.summary: A teacher of the assignment replaces its rubric with a new version: exactly {expectedVersion, criteria}, at most 32 KiB, sent as application/json. expectedVersion is the latest version the teacher saw (0 when none); another version added in between is 409 conflict. 1 to 12 criteria, each exactly {id, title, levels}: an id of 1 to 32 characters of a-z, 0-9, _ and -, unique in the list; a title of 1 to 120 characters; exactly three levels {label 1 to 80 characters, descriptor up to 400}; anything else, and any number, is 422 invalid_input. A stored version is never changed, so earlier versions stay as they were. The answer is the new {version, criteria}. A student, a teacher of another course, another institution and an unknown assignment are the same 404. The institution and the author come from the session, never from the body.

post.summary: teacher.submissions.get for many assignments in one snapshot (R1): one entry per distinct id, lowercase, in the order of first appearance. POST so the ids never land in a URL; the body is exactly {assignmentIds}, 0 to 500 UUIDs in any case (duplicates count), at most 32 KiB; any other key or a malformed id is 422 invalid_input. An assignment the caller does not teach, or that does not exist, is the same entry with an empty list, never 403 or 404; proving that over the database belongs to the handler. More than 500 assignments take several reads, each its own snapshot. A row the read cannot vouch for makes the whole answer 503.

200.description: an entry per assignment, possibly with no rows

put.summary: A teacher of the assignment's course switches the institution's work template on or off for the assignment: exactly {useInstitutionTemplate}, at most 1 KiB, sent as application/json. true freezes the latest version of the institution's template for the assignment's work type on the assignment and answers {useInstitutionTemplate: true, version}; when a version is already frozen it stays and is answered (a later version is not taken over); when the institution has no template for the work type yet it is 409 conflict. false removes the pin and answers {useInstitutionTemplate: false, version: null}, also when there was none. A version added to the institution's template later does not change a pin that is kept; switching off and on again takes the latest version, also after students began work. An assignment the caller does not teach, a mentorship assignment, an unknown and a malformed id are the same 404 (C-23); a body outside the contract is 422 invalid_input. Success follows the database commit.

200.description: the state of the template on the assignment

put.summary: Replaces text, kind and label of an entry of the caller's bank: {text, kind, label?} as when saving; a missing label or null leaves the entry without one. The creation time stays. Another teacher's entry and one that is not there answer 404 (an invalid body is refused first, as when saving); at most 4 KiB, sent as application/json.

anyOf.description: A short label of the teacher's, 1 to 40 characters, NFC; null or missing is none.

delete.summary: Removes an entry of the caller's bank. Another teacher's entry and one that is not there answer 404.

get.summary: The caller's own comment bank (N-03): saved comments, oldest first, at most 200. It belongs to its author alone (D-130); no one else, a student included, reads or lists it, and it is not part of any view of a work.

anyOf.description: A short label of the teacher's, 1 to 40 characters, NFC; null or missing is none.

post.summary: Saves a comment in the caller's bank: {text, kind}, kind one of must, sugg, q, praise; the text is as a comment's; at most 4 KiB, sent as application/json. At most 200 entries (422). Only a teacher whose role is confirmed may; every other caller gets 404.

anyOf.description: A short label of the teacher's, 1 to 40 characters, NFC; null or missing is none.

get.summary: A teacher of the course reads whether the assistant is switched on for the course, on by default. A student, a teacher of another course, an unknown or a malformed course returns 404.

200.description: the state of the course's switch

put.summary: Only a teacher of the course switches the assistant off or on for every assignment of the course, exactly {enabled}. Answers 200 with the state in force; setting the state in force changes nothing. Every change is recorded in the audit trail in the same transaction. A body that is not exactly this is 422. A student, a teacher of another course, an unknown or a malformed course returns 404.

get.summary: A teacher of the course reads its switch of the rhythm of typing, on by default, with who changed it last and when. It holds for every assignment of the course whose own switch is not set. A student, a teacher of another course, an unknown or a malformed course returns 404.

200.description: the state of the course's switch

put.summary: Only a teacher of the course switches the recording of the rhythm of typing off or on for the course, exactly {enabled}. It holds for every assignment of the course whose own switch is not set; an assignment's switch overrides it. Answers 200 with the new state and who changed it. Every switch is recorded in the audit trail in the same transaction. A body that is not exactly this is 422. A student, a teacher of another course, an unknown or a malformed course returns 404.

200.description: the new state of the course's switch

delete.summary: The holder of the course removes a required source from it; 204 also when there was none. A teacher that is not the holder, a student and a course the caller does not teach answer 404.

put.summary: The holder of the course adds a required source to it or changes one: {record, doi?, isbn?, undated?}, at most 64 KiB, as the student's source; the source id is chosen by the client and must equal record.id. A course holds at most 200 sources (422) and a DOI or an ISBN once (409 conflict). A teacher that is not the holder, a student and a course the caller does not teach answer 404.

get.summary: The required literature of a course, oldest first then by id, for a teacher of it. canWrite is true for the holder of the course and false for another teacher of it. A course the caller does not teach, a student, an unknown and a malformed id all answer 404. A student of the course reads it in student.course-literature.get.

The course roster and the state of each student's work per assignment. Course teachers see the course; group teachers see their own groups. A missing name pair or group is null. A document id links to the work when one exists. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed course id returns the same empty list as a course with no students.

The teacher's courses and their assignments (institution.list_teacher_courses). Courses by academic year descending, then name (hr collation), then id; assignments by due time, then title, then id. Each course carries its rule on AI help, which a new assignment may only keep or narrow.

post.summary: The teacher of the assignment extends its deadline for one student of it (scope one) or for all (scope all). dueAt must be later than the deadline in force; the reason all is only for scope all. existingSubmissionsUnchanged is true when a submission in the scope was already recorded: the extension leaves it as it is. Success follows the database commit. An inaccessible assignment or student returns 404; invalid input or an earlier deadline 422.

get.summary: The deadline extensions of an assignment, oldest first, for its teacher. reasonId is null on a record another teacher wrote. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.

One AI assistant conversation the student attached to the declaration bound to the live submission, for the course teacher: the messages by seq from 1 to the throughSeq the student confirmed, with the messagesSha256 the declaration carries. A conversation the bound declaration does not attach (unattached, another student's, another assignment's, unknown or malformed id), an assignment or student the teacher has no access to, and a work without a live submission return the same 404; a mentor is refused alike. Opening it is recorded in the access log. A stored conversation that no longer matches what the student confirmed is 503.

The optional question the teacher asks with the declaration of the assignment (null: none), and when it was last changed, for the teacher of the assignment. A student, another teacher, an unknown or a malformed assignment returns 404.

anyOf.description: Up to 500 Unicode code points, NFC, no leading or trailing space, no control character but the line feed.

put.summary: The teacher of the assignment sets the optional question asked with the declaration, exactly {question}: a text of up to 500 code points, or null to remove it. It may change after the assignment is published; every change is recorded with its author and time in the same transaction, and setting the question in force changes nothing. An answer already saved keeps the question it answered. A body that is not exactly this is 422. A student, another teacher, an unknown or a malformed assignment returns 404.

anyOf.description: Up to 500 Unicode code points, NFC, no leading or trailing space, no control character but the line feed.
Up to 500 Unicode code points, NFC, no leading or trailing space, no control character but the line feed.

get.summary: Whether a submission of the assignment requires a declaration confirmed for the submitted revision (off by default), and when it was last changed, for the teacher of the assignment. A student, another teacher, an unknown or a malformed assignment returns 404.

put.summary: The teacher of the assignment turns the required declaration on or off, exactly {required}. While it is on, a submission without a declaration confirmed for the submitted revision is refused (submission.submit-second.post 409 declaration_required). Every change is recorded with its author and time in the same transaction; setting the value in force changes nothing and returns it. A submission already recorded stays. A body that is not exactly this is 422. A student, another teacher, an unknown or a malformed assignment returns 404.

get.summary: The declaration a student bound to the live submission of the named assignment, for the course teacher. Without a live submission the state is none. An assignment, student or relationship the teacher has no access to returns 404. Opening a bound declaration is recorded in the access log.

200.description: the bound declaration with its hash, or none

text.description: Up to 2000 Unicode code points, NFC, no leading or trailing space, no control character but the line feed.
Up to 2000 Unicode code points, NFC, no leading or trailing space, no control character but the line feed.

post.summary: The teacher's fast path through the works of one assignment (B-11, #757): per student the state of the work, its text as blocks and the same process summary the student sees. POST so the assignment id never lands in a URL; the body is exactly {assignmentId}, a UUID in any case, at most 1 KiB; any other key or a malformed id is 422 invalid_input. An assignment the caller does not teach, or that does not exist, is the same empty list, never 403 or 404. Named students by surname, given name (hr) and id, then the unnamed by id.

delete.summary: The teacher of the assignment (of its course, or its mentor) clears the assignment's own switch of the rhythm of typing, so that the switch of its course holds again (on by default). No body. Answers 200 with the state that now holds and its source. A clearing is recorded in the audit trail in the same transaction; clearing a switch nobody set changes nothing. A student, another teacher, an unknown or a malformed assignment returns 404.

get.summary: The teacher of the assignment (of its course, or its mentor) reads the switch of the rhythm of typing, on by default, with who changed it last and when. A student, another teacher, an unknown or a malformed assignment returns 404.

put.summary: Only the teacher of the assignment (of its course, or its mentor) switches the recording of the rhythm of typing off or on for every work of it, exactly {enabled}. Switching off holds from that moment: nothing is recorded and nothing is read while it is off; what was recorded stays until it is deleted or due. Answers 200 with the new state and who changed it. Every switch is recorded in the audit trail in the same transaction. A body that is not exactly this is 422. A student, another teacher, an unknown or a malformed assignment returns 404.

200.description: the new state of the switch

post.summary: The teacher of the assignment records that one student of it may still submit until untilAt, with a reason from the closed list. untilAt must be later than now, than the deadline that holds for the student and than the student's earlier exception. The record is never changed or removed and its audit row is written by the same command. Success follows the database commit. An inaccessible assignment or student returns 404; invalid input or a time that is not later 422.

get.summary: The late-submission exceptions of an assignment, oldest first, for its teacher. reasonId is null on a record another teacher wrote. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.

put.summary: The holder of the course (or the mentor of a mentorship work) marks that the literature of the work was reviewed. No body. One mark per work: a later one replaces the earlier, and seenAt is the time of the database clock, as the guidance reads it. A reader that is not a writer, the student of the work and an inaccessible work answer 404.

post.summary: The confirmed teacher to whom an open request was made approves or declines it. An optional decline reason has 1 to 600 Unicode code points and contains a non-whitespace character. It is kept in the audit record. Success follows the database commit; a closed request returns 409.

get.summary: The open mentorship requests made to the confirmed, unrevoked teacher in the caller's institution. A student without a name pair has a null name. The decision reason stays in the audit record.
One open mentorship of the caller as mentor. Another institution's, an ended one, an unknown and a malformed id all read the same 404.
The open mentorships of the caller as mentor, newest first; anyone else gets the same empty list. No time, activity or count of a work.

The ZIP of a ready Merlin package as application/zip, for the teacher who asked for it while teaching the assignment, before its expiry; the download is recorded in the same transaction that reads the bytes. The ZIP holds merlin-popis.csv (teacher.merlin-roster-csv.get), the PDF and DOCX of every submitted work under the names the CSV gives, and otisci.sha256 (one line per file: SHA-256, two spaces, name). Content-Disposition names the file merlin-paket.zip; X-Content-SHA256 is the SHA-256 of the ZIP, as teacher.merlin-package.get names it. A package not yet built or failed returns 409, an expired one 410; errors as teacher.merlin-package.get, as JSON.

200.description: ZIP bytes (application/zip); the contract format has no binary body

get.summary: The state of a Merlin package the caller asked for, while the caller teaches the assignment. A ready package names its download path, its expiry (24 hours after the build) and the SHA-256 of the ZIP; an expired one its expiry and SHA-256, without a path. A package of another teacher, of another assignment, unknown or malformed returns 404; a cross-site read 403.

post.summary: The teacher of the assignment asks for its Merlin package with a request key of the client's (8 to 128 of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, - and _). A new key makes a package and the server builds it; the same key again answers the same package and never builds a second one (a failed package is built again). The answer follows the build: ready, failed, or queued while another request is building it; expired once 24 hours have passed since the build. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment returns 404.

get.summary: The rows of teacher.merlin-roster.get as text/csv; charset=utf-8 (RFC 4180, CRLF, UTF-8 byte order mark): a header from the message catalogue (locales/merlin.ts) and the same columns in the same order. A null is an empty cell, true and false are the catalogue's yes and no words; a cell a spreadsheet would read as a formula starts with an apostrophe. No extension reasons. Content-Disposition names the file merlin-popis.csv. Errors as teacher.merlin-roster.get, as JSON.

200.description: CSV bytes (text/csv; charset=utf-8); the contract format has no text body

get.summary: The Merlin roster of an assignment for its teacher (D-286): one row per student by surname (Croatian alphabet), then given name; a student without a name pair last. Columns: surname, given name, submitted, the submission minute, after the deadline (with an approved extension, as the submission recorded it), and the names and SHA-256 fingerprints of the PDF and DOCX of the submitted revision in the package; null for a student without a submission. extensionReasons are the caller's own deadline extension records (N-13), oldest first. Nothing from the process summary and no private criterion. The read writes the teacher's opening of each work to the access log. A cross-site read is 403; an inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment 404; reads that disagree 503.

200.description: the roster, possibly with no rows

get.summary: The answers of a questionnaire as questionnaire-export-v1, for a teacher of its course: {schema, questionnaireId, variables[{questionId, order, kind, label, options}], rows[{n, values{questionId: value|null}}], responseCount, includesText}. A row is one sheet with no person and no time; n is the position of the sheet in the order of a hash of its id, never of the time it came in, and the same sheets give the same bytes. A question without an answer on a sheet is null. Free-text questions are left out (includesText false) unless the query is includeText=true; any other value of includeText is 422 invalid_input, and any other parameter is 422 too. A read that is not same-origin (Sec-Fetch-Site other than same-origin) is 403 forbidden. Fewer sheets than the least number for an export (5) is 409 conflict and returns nothing. The export has no grade, rank, sum or comparison of a person and is not sent to any service; the web builds CSV from it. A student, a teacher of another course, an unknown and a malformed questionnaire id return the same 404.

post.summary: A teacher of the course enters one sheet by hand (invented or on paper), exactly {answers[{questionId, value}]} as a student sends it. The sheet has no person and no participation is recorded, so it does not stop any student from answering. Only while the questionnaire is open: a draft or a closed questionnaire is 409 conflict. An answer that does not fit its question is 422. A student, a teacher of another course, an unknown or a malformed questionnaire id returns 404.

A teacher of the course moves a questionnaire one step on: exactly {state}, open (from draft) or closed (from open); there is no way back. Any other step is 409 conflict. The answer is {id, state}. A teacher of another course, another institution, a student, an unknown and a malformed id all read the same 404.

get.summary: One questionnaire with its questions in order, for a teacher of its course. A teacher of another course, another institution, a student, an unknown and a malformed id all read the same 404.

patch.summary: A teacher of the course replaces the title and the questions of a questionnaire that is still a draft (the same {title, questions} as the POST). An open or closed questionnaire is 409 conflict and is not changed. A teacher of another course, another institution, a student, an unknown and a malformed id all read the same 404.

get.summary: The questionnaires of a course for its teacher, newest first: {questionnaires: [{id, title, state, createdOn, questionCount, responseCount}]}. responseCount is a number, never a list of people. A teacher of another course, another institution, a student, an unknown and a malformed id all read the same 404.

post.summary: A teacher of the course makes a questionnaire in the draft state: exactly {title, questions}, at most 256 KiB, application/json. title is one line of 1 to 200 characters; questions are 1 to 40, each exactly {kind, text, options?, scale?}: kind is single, multiple, scale, number or text; text is one line of 1 to 500 characters; options (2 to 20 of {code, label}, distinct codes) only for single and multiple; scale ({min, max}, whole numbers 0 to 10, min below max) only for scale. The order is the array's. The answer is the new questionnaire with the ids of its questions. A body outside this is 422 invalid_input. A teacher of another course, another institution, a student, an unknown and a malformed id all read the same 404.

get.summary: Download the same PDF as the student, for a reader authorized to see this submission. No signed receipt, no relation to the work or a malformed id returns 404.

200.description: PDF bytes encoded in standard Base64, with a download filename

get.summary: The guidance on the sources of one work, for a reader of it: every source of the work, oldest first then by id (the student's own and the recommended or required ones, each with the number of proofs attached to it), the proof requests oldest first (open and closed), and literatureSeenAt, the time a teacher marked the literature of the work as reviewed (null before). canWrite is true for the holder of the course and the mentor of a mentorship work and false for every other reader; the page offers the writes only then. The student of the work, another teacher, an unknown work and a malformed id all read the same 404.

The JPEG bytes of one proof of a source of a work, for any reader of the work. The proof is named by its work, source and id together; another work's, another source's, an unknown or a malformed id and a caller that does not read the work answer 404.

200.description: the JPEG bytes of the excerpt

delete.summary: The holder of the course (or the mentor of a mentorship work) closes the open request for a proof of a source; the request stays in the history with its closing time. 204 also when there was no open request. A reader that is not a writer and an inaccessible work answer 404.

put.summary: The holder of the course (or the mentor of a mentorship work) asks the student for a proof of a source of the work: {instruction, dueAt}, at most 4 KiB; dueAt is an instant in the future (Date.toISOString). An open request of that source is changed, otherwise a new one is made, so a source has at most one open request. The student reads it in student.source-proof-requests.get. A source that is not in the work, a reader that is not a writer and an inaccessible work answer 404. An instruction that is empty, over 1000 code points or holds a control character, and a deadline that is not in the future, is 422.

get.summary: The proofs (attached excerpts) of one source of a work, oldest first then by id, for any reader of the work (the holder, a collaborator, a seminar group teacher, the mentor). The student of the work reads them in student.source-proofs.get. A source that is not in the work, the student of the work, another teacher, an unknown work and a malformed id all answer 404.

delete.summary: The holder of the course (or the mentor of a mentorship work) removes a recommended or required source from the work, with its proofs, notes and proof requests; 204 also when there was none. A source of the student (without a requirement) is not removed here and answers 404, as does a reader that is not a writer and an inaccessible work.

put.summary: The holder of the course of a work (or the mentor of a mentorship work) recommends or requires a source on the work: {record, requirement: recommended | required, doi?, isbn?, undated?}, at most 64 KiB, as the student's source of student.work-sources.put; the source id is chosen by the client and must equal record.id. The same id again changes it. The student reads it in the work's source list with its requirement. A work holds at most 500 sources. A collaborator or any other reader that is not a writer, the student of the work, a source of the student (without a requirement) and an inaccessible work answer 404. A record that does not fit its shape, a requirement outside the two or a full list is 422.

get.summary: The immutable submitted document of a student in the named assignment. The teacher must have access to the work. Missing or inaccessible submissions return 404. Opening the submitted document is recorded in the access log.

200.description: the submitted version and the lateness recorded at submission

document.description: The exact UTF-8 JSON text of the submitted document.

get.summary: One student's submissions and withdrawals of the assignment, oldest first, each with its signed receipt (null while not bound), for a reader of the work (as teacher.submission-detail.get). The last valid submission is the last submission event not followed by a withdrawal. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed id returns 404.

The same submission state and signed receipt as student.submission.get, for a student the caller may read. The read has no work content and writes nothing to the access log (P-5). Inaccessible, unknown and malformed ids return the same 404.
Whether students may withdraw their submissions of the assignment (allowed by default), for its teacher. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.

post.summary: The teacher of the assignment switches withdrawal off or on. Setting the value in force changes nothing and returns it. A withdrawal already recorded stays. An inaccessible, unknown or malformed assignment id returns 404.

The teacher of the assignment asks for a link to the ZIP of all its submissions, with the works as PDF (format pdf) or DOCX (format docx). The answer is the download path with the link token and its expiry, 24 hours after the request; asking again issues a new link and changes nothing stored. The request reads no work and writes nothing. Another's, an unknown or a malformed assignment returns 404.

get.summary: Download through a link from teacher.submissions-bulk-link.post, within its 24 hours and with the session that asked for it, while the caller teaches the assignment. The body is application/zip (predaje.zip): for every submitted work of this assignment and no other, the work as <name>.pdf or <name>.docx and its signed receipt as <name>-potvrda.pdf (absent while the receipt awaits its signature), and otisci.sha256 with the SHA-256 of every file. Every download writes the opening of each submitted text to the access log. X-Content-SHA256 is the SHA-256 of the body. A link of another assignment, format or session, or an assignment the caller does not teach, is 404, an expired link 410, a cross-site read 403.

200.description: ZIP bytes (application/zip); the contract format has no binary body

get.summary: Which students of an assignment submitted, with the work each row links to, for the assignment's teacher; one row per student with an open membership, by student id. Anyone else, an unknown or a malformed id gets the same empty list. No text, name, exact time, deadline, hash or submission id.

put.summary: Sets the level and the note of one criterion of the latest rubric version, replacing both: exactly {level, note}, at most 8 KiB, sent as application/json. level is 0, 1, 2 or null, note 1 to 2000 characters or null; a null for both clears the mark. Anything else, and any other number, is 422 invalid_input. Answers the saved {criterionId, level, note}. Only the teacher of the work; the student, another teacher, an unknown work and a criterion that is not in the latest rubric version read the same 404. The author comes from the session, never from the body.

get.summary: The caller's own marks on a work for the latest rubric version of its assignment: {rubricVersion, marks}, one {criterionId, level, note} per criterion in the rubric's order, level 0, 1, 2 or null and note or null where nothing is set. rubricVersion is 0 and the marks cover the six default criteria while the teacher set no rubric. No number, sum, grade or rank. Only the teacher of the work who wrote the marks reads them; the student of the work, another teacher, a teacher of another course, another institution, an unknown work and a malformed id all read the same 404. The read writes nothing in the access log.

200.description: the marks of the latest rubric version

get.summary: The contribution of one team, the same answer and the same bytes as student.work-team-contribution.get for a member of that team (the student sees what the teacher sees). It never orders teams or members by an amount and names no person above another. Read by the teachers of the course; another's, an unknown or a malformed assignment or team reads 404.

200.description: the contribution state of the team

post.summary: The teacher adds an enrolled student to the team or removes one from it. Each is added to the record of the team and nothing is deleted. A student already in a team, a team above maxSize, teams off and removing a student whose own part was submitted are 409 conflict. A student not enrolled, a team of another assignment or an unknown id reads 404; a malformed id in the path is 404, a malformed studentId in the body is 422 invalid_input.

get.summary: The teams of the assignment and the enrolled students without a team. Members and unassigned students are in the order of family name, then given name, then studentId; teams by the first member in that order, then teamId. A member carries the state of their own part as a fact (not_started, in_progress, submitted). It is a list of facts: no count of points, no comparison, no state of good or bad. Read by the teachers of the course; another's, an unknown or a malformed assignment reads 404.

200.description: the teams and the students without a team

post.summary: The teacher creates an empty team on the assignment, to add students to it (teams formed by the teacher need it; the route is added to the task's list as the smallest contract that makes teacher_assigned usable). With teams off it is 409 conflict. Another's, an unknown or a malformed assignment reads 404.

get.summary: One work by its document id: the student's id and display name (null when the account has no name), the assignment, the state of the submission and the previous and next work of the same assignment among the works the caller may read, in the order of the assignment overview (null at either end). Only a reader of the work; the student, another teacher, an unknown work and a malformed id all read the same 404. The read has no text of the work and writes nothing in the access log.

The six criteria of the caller's own working note on a work, always in the same order, with a null assessment and note where nothing is set. Only the teacher of the work who wrote them reads them; the student, another teacher, an unknown work and a malformed id all read the same 404. The read writes nothing in the access log.

put.summary: Sets the assessment and the note of one criterion, replacing both: a null clears it, and a criterion with neither reads as not set. Answers the saved criterion. Only the teacher of the work; the student, another teacher, an unknown work and an unknown criterion read the same 404.

get.summary: Who opened the caller's own work and when (PRODUCT §5 rule 17, plan M10.4): one row per stored opening of five minutes, grouped into Europe/Zagreb days, the newest day and the newest row first. Rows are never merged; there is no total of visits, no duration and no count per day (D-274 MQ10). Only the owner of the work reads it; another's work, an unknown and a malformed id read the same 404 (C-23). The query names the oldest row shown, beforeAt and beforeId from next; a page from it holds only windows strictly older, so a day can continue on the next page. Only both together, on the five-minute grid, a lowercase UUID and not in the future are a cursor; anything else, and any other parameter, reads the first page with continued false, never an error. A row the read cannot vouch for makes the whole answer 503.

200.description: a page of openings in days, possibly none

post.summary: The student who owns the work explains one finding of the match with the assistant, exactly {segmentRef, messageId, text}: the text 1 to 2000 characters, NFC, not blank, no control character but newline and tab. Written once per finding and never rewritten; a second explanation of the same finding is 409. Answers 201 with the explanation and when it was written. A body that is not exactly this is 422. A finding that does not exist, anyone but the owner of the work, and any request while the faculty's switch is off get 404. It is not evidence of authorship.

get.summary: The segments of a work that match an answer of the assistant of the same work in 8 or more words in a row, oldest first: the segment reference, the ids of the conversation and of the answer and the length of the run, never a text. The same answer for the student who owns the work and for its readers. An empty list while the faculty's switch is off. It is not evidence of authorship. Another's, an unknown or a malformed work returns 404.

post.summary: The student who owns the work sends a segment, exactly {segmentRef, text} (text 1 to 40000 characters), and it is compared with the answers of the assistant in the student's own conversations of the same assignment (8 or more words in a row, normalization of case, spacing and punctuation). Each answer that matches is recorded once as a finding and its conversation is attached as transferred text (D-41). Answers 200 with the matches (ids and the length of the run), possibly none; with the faculty's switch off, always none and nothing is saved. A body that is not exactly this is 422. Anyone but the owner of the work gets 404.

200.description: the matches of this segment, possibly none

get.summary: Read an attachment as standard Base64 after authorization against the work that owns the attachment and verification of the stored bytes. An unknown or inaccessible attachment returns 404.

200.description: Verified image bytes and attachment reference

post.summary: Upload a PNG or JPEG of up to 5 MiB with standard Base64. The server derives the type and SHA-256 from the bytes. Repeating the same bytes in the same work returns the existing attachment.

get.summary: What the student changed since the caller's last review (N-05): the difference by blocks between the reviewed revision and the current one, from the version comparison of SRV-9E, every block once as unchanged, removed or added, in order, at most 5000 per version. reviewedRevision is null before the first review (no baseline: changed is false and blocks is empty); when nothing changed since, changed is false and blocks is empty. Read like a replay, so a teacher's read writes a row of the access log. Only a teacher of the work may; every other caller gets 404.

200.description: the changes since the last review

delete.summary: Removes a draft of the caller. A thread left with no published comment goes with its last draft. A published comment, another's draft and one that is not there all answer 404.

get.summary: The caller's own unpublished comments on a work (D-51), in the order of their threads, at most 1000. Only a teacher of the work has any; the student and everyone else get the same 404 as for a work that is not there (C-23). A draft is read by no one but its author until it is published.

post.summary: Writes a draft the student does not see until the teacher publishes (D-51): {text, anchor} opens a draft thread on a paragraph (201 {threadId}), {threadId, text} drafts a reply to a thread of the work (201 {commentId}); a reply to a resolved thread is 409. The text is 1 to 2000 characters with a non-space, NFC, no control character but newline and tab, no bidi control; at most 8 KiB, sent as application/json. At most 500 drafts of one teacher on one work (422). Only a teacher of the work may; every other caller gets 404.

201.description: the new draft: its thread for a new one, its comment for a reply

post.summary: Publishes the caller's drafts on the work as work.comments.publish.post does, but only when {draftIds} names exactly the comment ids of those drafts (the ones the teacher saw); any difference, or no draft, is 409 and nothing is published. Sent as application/json, at most 32 KiB. Only a teacher of the work may; every other caller gets 404.

Gives every draft of the caller on the work to the student at one instant (D-51) and answers how many. A teacher's published reply makes an answered thread open. No draft is 409. Only a teacher of the work may; every other caller gets 404. No body.

get.summary: The difference by blocks between revision from and revision to (from < to) of a work, rebuilt by the server from the verified record, not from saved texts: every block of both versions once as unchanged, removed or added, in order, at most 5000 blocks per version. The owner and a teacher of the work get the same answer; a teacher's read writes a row of the access log. A work or revision the caller may not read, or the record does not hold, returns 404; equal or reversed revisions and a missing or extra query parameter return 422; a record that cannot be replayed or a comparison too large returns 503.

200.description: the difference between the two revisions

post.summary: Adds a text to a consultation record of the work. Exactly {text}, at most 8 KiB. An empty or blank text is 422; a record that is not this work's reads as 404. Answers 201 with the addition and its whole-minute time.

get.summary: The consultation records of a work, oldest meeting first, each with its additions in the order they were made. The same list for the owner and the teacher of the assignment. Another's, an unknown or a malformed work returns 404.

post.summary: Records a consultation about a work: the day it was held, the revision it is about (a revision of the same work), a topic and the agreement. Exactly those four fields, at most 8 KiB. An empty topic, a date that does not exist or a revision of another work is 422. Answers 201 with the record, which has no additions yet.

Closes a consultation slot, with an optional reason (1 to 600 code points). withdraw: the owning student, while the teacher has not answered (requested). decline: the teacher of the work, while requested. cancel: either side, a countered or confirmed slot whose time lies ahead. The wrong side is 403, a state that does not allow the move 409.

get.summary: Every consultation slot of the work, closed ones included, ordered by startsAt and id, with the topic, the closing and the preparation. Only the student who owns the work and the teacher of the work read it; anyone else is 403. work.consultation-slots.get stays as it is and leaves closed slots out.

post.summary: The owning student requests a consultation at a time within a year, with an optional topic (1 to 200 code points) and an optional preparation: a text of up to 4000 code points and the counts of changed paragraphs and resolved comments, all three or none. The preparation is a record of input, not of authorship; only the student and the teacher of the work read it. At most 20 open requests a work (422).

get.summary: List the consultation slots of an accessible work, ordered by startsAt and id. proposedAt is the instant the student first requested the slot.

post.summary: The owning student requests a consultation at the given time.

patch.summary: The teacher confirms or replaces startsAt with a counter-proposal. The owning student accepts that time. proposedAt remains the instant of the original request.

post.summary: The teacher of the work marks an agreed task done or not done: exactly {done}. A mark is added, never changed; a mark equal to the current state adds nothing. For the student and anyone else this is 404.

get.summary: The agreed tasks of every consultation record of the work, by record (oldest meeting first) and position, each with its state (the newest mark). The same list for the student who owns the work and the teacher of the work; another's, an unknown or a malformed work is 404.

post.summary: The teacher of the work (the mentor) adds an agreed task to a consultation record of the work: exactly {text}, 1 to 500 code points, not blank. At most 20 a record (422). The student reads the tasks and never writes them; for the student, another's work and a record of another work this is 404. A task is never changed or deleted.

get.summary: The direct-edit setting of a work and its record, the same for the student of the work and every teacher of its assignment: mode (suggestions, the default, or direct), changedAt (null when never changed) and the record oldest first, at most the last 1000 entries: each change of the mode (source student) and each accepted direct edit (source teacher, its size in bytes). Times are in the 5-minute window of P-03. Another's, an unknown or a malformed work returns 404.

put.summary: The student owner sets the direct-edit mode of the work: {mode: "direct"} turns direct edits of its teachers on, {mode: "suggestions"} revokes them at once and without the other side. Sent as application/json, at most 1 KiB. The value is absolute: the same mode again answers unchanged and writes nothing. 200 {outcome, mode, changedAt}. While the mode is direct, a teacher of the work publishes an edit with live.document.put and `If-Match: "<etag>"`, the ETag of the state read (64 hex): the edit replaces exactly that state and is recorded as the teacher's; a teacher's 409 always carries a null token, and with suggestions the teacher's put is 404. A teacher, another's, an unknown, a malformed or a submitted work returns 404; another mode is 422.

200.description: applied, or the same mode again

get.summary: The amendments and disputes of the events of a work's process summary, oldest first, for the student who owns the work and for the readers of it. The process summary itself is unchanged. Another's, an unknown or a malformed work returns 404.

post.summary: The student who owns the work amends or disputes one event of its process summary: exactly {kind, eventId, text}, at most 4 KiB. A kind other than amendment or dispute, an event id that is not one or a text of no characters, only blanks or over 1000 characters is 422. A reader of the work who is not its owner is 403; another's, an unknown or a malformed work is 404. Answers 201 with the id and the time of the record; the process summary is unchanged.

get.summary: Download the submitted or last saved revision as the owner or supervising teacher. The report hash is present only for certified bytes.

Download one sheet of a spreadsheet work as CSV: UTF-8 with a byte order mark, semicolon between cells, CRLF line ends, the computed value of every cell (formulas are computed again on the server). A text that starts with = + - @ a tab or a carriage return gets a leading apostrophe. sheet is the id of a sheet of the work; without it the first sheet is exported. A teacher's read writes the access log, as work.export.get does. Another's, an unknown or a malformed work, a work that is not a spreadsheet and an unknown sheet return 404.

200.description: the CSV bytes of the sheet

get.summary: Download one saved version of a spreadsheet work as an .xlsx (OOXML, no macros): every sheet, the text and number of each cell, and each formula with the value the server computed again (an error is its code, such as #DIV/0!). The same version gives the same bytes and the same X-Export-Sheet-Sha256 (the SHA-256 of the canonical sheet document, lowercase hex). versionId is a revision from work.versions.get; without it the newest saved version is exported. A teacher's read writes the access log, as the versions list does. Another's, an unknown or a malformed work, an unknown version and a work that is not a spreadsheet return 404.

Download one saved version of a slides work as a .pptx or a PDF. The .pptx is written from the frozen snapshot of the version: the same version gives the same bytes and the same X-Export-Snapshot-Sha256 (the SHA-256 of the snapshot, lowercase hex). The PDF is converted from that .pptx by the local converter and carries the same snapshot hash, but its own bytes are not promised to be identical between requests; it is never marked PDF/A. format is pptx or pdf. versionId is a revision from work.versions.get; without it the newest saved version is exported. A teacher's read writes the access log, as the versions list does. Another's, an unknown or a malformed work, an unknown version and a work that is not a slides work return 404; a format outside the list returns 422; a conversion that is not available, times out or fails, and an image the version binds that cannot be printed, return 503.

200.description: the .pptx or the PDF bytes of the version

get.summary: Download one saved version of a work as a DOCX, rendered from its frozen export snapshot: the same version gives the same bytes and the same X-Export-Snapshot-Sha256 (the SHA-256 of the snapshot, lowercase hex). format is docx; pdf is not ready and returns 422. versionId is a revision from work.versions.get; without it the newest saved version is exported. A teacher's read writes the access log, as the versions list does. Another's, an unknown or a malformed work, and an unknown version, return 404.

200.description: the DOCX bytes of the version

post.summary: The student owner confirms a reviewed import: {importId, manifestSha256} as application/json, at most 1 KiB, the importId equal to the one in the path. The first confirmation and every retry answer the same 200 {importId, eventId}: one import gives exactly one event, also when two tabs confirm at once. Another's, a teacher's, an unknown or a malformed import is 404 import_not_found; another reviewed hash 409 import_manifest_mismatch; after 60 minutes 410 import_expired; an assignment that no longer allows import or a submitted work 403 import_not_allowed; a revision committed since the preview 409 import_revision_changed. A confirmed import stays confirmed.

200.description: confirmed, or the same confirmation again

post.summary: The student owner sends a DOCX or PDF as standard Base64, at most 2 MiB (2 097 152 bytes), with the file name or null, as application/json. The server reads the DOCX or the PDF text layer within the import limits. Active content is refused. 201 is a preview: importId, SHA-256 of the canonical manifest ductus-import-manifest-v1, source import, evidenceKind imported, fileFormat, content as document v2, DOCX traces (empty for PDF), rawByteLength, the normalised file name or null, baseRevision and expiresAt (60 minutes). Confirm it with work.imports.confirm.post. A file above the limit is 413 body_too_large, a PDF without text is 422 pdf_no_text_layer, other reader refusals are 422 invalid_document, and an assignment without import allowed or a submitted work is 403 import_not_allowed. A teacher, another's, an unknown or a malformed work is 404.

201.description: the preview of the import, waiting for the student's confirmation

get.summary: Whether the rhythm of typing is recorded for this work: the state of the teacher's switch of its assignment, on by default, with who changed it last (teacher or mentor, and the name when known) and when, both null while the default holds. The student reads it and cannot change it. The same answer for the owner and the readers of the work. Another's, an unknown or a malformed work returns 404.

delete.summary: The student who owns the work deletes its recorded rhythm on request, also while the recording is off. No body. Answers 200 with the number of bursts deleted, possibly 0. Anyone but the owner of the work gets 404.

get.summary: The recorded bursts of a work, oldest first: the gaps in milliseconds and the time of each, nothing derived from them. The same answer for the student who owns the work and for its readers. None while the teacher has switched the recording off. It is a record of input, not of authorship. Another's, an unknown or a malformed work returns 404.

post.summary: The student who owns the work records one burst, exactly {gapsMs}: 1 to 130 whole gaps in milliseconds (0 to 3600000) between inputs, never a key or a content. Answers 200 {recorded: true}, or {recorded: false} while the teacher has switched the recording off: then nothing is saved. A body that is not exactly this is 422. Anyone but the owner of the work gets 404.

put.summary: Sets the appointment: a consultation slot of the work (the teacher, or the student after the invitation) or a free place and time ahead (the teacher). A held interview takes no new appointment (409).

post.summary: The owning student explains, in general or about one question, after the invitation. At most 100 explanations per work.
A teacher of the work notes the date the interview was held, once, after the invitation, not in the future. The outcome is not recorded here.
Makes the questions visible to the student from this instant and writes the invitation to the trail. A teacher with no question of their own, or a second invitation, is 409. No body.

The owning student attaches a note to the preparation after the invitation: a UTF-8 text or a PDF of at most 1 MiB in standard Base64. The server derives the size and the SHA-256 and writes the attachment to the trail; the same bytes again answer the note already kept. Before the invitation, another student and a teacher get 403, a held interview 409, a work at 20 notes 422.

get.summary: The PDF of the interview preparation of an accessible work: the same questions, explanations, appointment and date the student reads, under the notice that the preparation is no accusation and no disciplinary proceeding. Before the invitation there is nothing the student reads, so it is 409. Anyone who may not read the preparation gets 403.

200.description: PDF bytes encoded in standard Base64, with a download filename

delete.summary: Removes a question: its author before the invitation, a teacher of the work after it. Anyone else, and an unknown question, get 403.

post.summary: A teacher or mentor of the work adds a question, about a paragraph or general (paragraphRef null or absent). At most 50 questions per work.

get.summary: The interview preparation of an accessible work: questions, invitation, explanations, appointment and the date it was held. Before the invitation only the author of a question reads it and the owning student reads nothing (403). A work with no preparation answers an empty one.

The mentor's consent to the submission of this thesis (none, given, withdrawn), who changed it, when and with what comment, every change in order, and the faculty's switch. The student sees what the mentor sees.

put.summary: The mentor gives (given = true) or withdraws the consent, with an optional comment. Giving it while it is given, or withdrawing it while it is not, is 409. Anyone else is 403.

get.summary: The short messages of a work, oldest first in the order of writing (the same order on every reading), at most 1000: the same conversation for the student of the work and the teachers of its assignment. senderRole is the role the author had when writing. Another's, an unknown or a malformed work returns 404.

post.summary: Writes a short message to the conversation of a work: {text}, 1 to 2000 characters with a non-space, NFC, no control character but newline and tab, no bidi control, at most 4 KiB, sent as application/json. It answers 201 with the stored message, as the list gives it. An empty or blank message is 422 and writes nothing; so is the 1001st message of a work. The student of the work and the teachers of its assignment write; another's, an unknown or a malformed work returns 404.

The mentor of a work adds a milestone at the end of its plan: {title, dueAt?, submits}, at most 2 KiB. The answer is the whole plan. Not after the final submission of the work (409), at most 100 milestones (409). A student and a teacher who is not the mentor of the work are 403.

201.description: The plan of the work with the new milestone

post.summary: The mentor of a work replaces its milestones with the latest template of the institution. No body. Refused (409) once any milestone of the work was ever submitted, after the final submission, and while the institution has no template. A student and a teacher who is not the mentor of the work are 403. The answer is the whole plan.

200.description: The plan of the work from the template

get.summary: The milestones of one work as they are configured, in workflow order, with what each sends (submits) and the deadline of this work, for its owner and teachers. The student sees what the mentor sees. The state of each milestone is work.milestone-states.get.
The milestones of one work in workflow order with the state of each (not_submitted, submitted, revision_requested, approved), for its owner and teachers. The student sees what the mentor sees.

200.description: Milestones with the current deadlines and states of this work

post.summary: The mentor of the work approves a submitted milestone, with an optional short message.

delete.summary: The mentor deletes a milestone that was never submitted. A milestone that was ever submitted answers 409: it can only be renamed.

patch.summary: A teacher changes the deadline of one configured milestone of an unsubmitted work.

A teacher changes the title and/or the deadline of one milestone, also after it was sent. The deadline does not change after the final submission (409); a title changes only on the assignment of a mentorship (409 elsewhere).

get.summary: The configured milestones of one work, in workflow order, for its owner and teachers.

200.description: Configured milestones with the current deadlines of this work

post.summary: The mentor of the work asks for a revision of a submitted milestone. The comment is required; revisionDueAt is a reminder and never blocks writing or submitting.

The student owner sends a milestone for review. The revision of the work at this moment is frozen as a reference (submittedRevisionId); no content is copied. Only from not_submitted or revision_requested; the milestone deadline is a reminder and never blocks.

get.summary: The share of the characters of a work per kind of origin (typed, assistant_inserted, assistant_match, imported_file, pasted_known, pasted_unknown), always all six in this order, all 0 while nothing is recorded. The same answer for the student who owns the work and for its readers. It is a record of where text came from, not of who wrote it. Another's, an unknown or a malformed work returns 404.

The ranges of origin of one revision of a work, in the order recorded: the block (its node id), the range of code points of the block's text (start inclusive, end exclusive), the kind from the same closed list as work.origin-composition.get, and the segmentRef of work.assistant-match.post when the range was recorded with one (null otherwise), so a finding of the match resolves to its ranges. The ranges are those of the latest recorded revision at or below ?revision (the latest of all without it); revision names it, null with no ranges while none is recorded. A paste explained later reads pasted_known. The same answer for the student who owns the work and for its readers. It says where text came from, not who wrote it. A revision that is not a whole number up to 2^53-1 is 422. Another's, an unknown or a malformed work returns 404.

200.description: the ranges of the revision, possibly none

post.summary: The student who owns the work records the ranges of origin of one revision they saved, exactly {revision, segments}: 1 to 10000 ranges, each {blockId, start, end, kind, segmentRef?, changeId?} as work.origin-segments.get reads them, end above start; pasted_known only with the changeId of an explained change of the same kind. Recorded once per revision and never rewritten: a second write of the same revision is 409. Answers 201 with the revision and the number of ranges recorded. A body that is not exactly this, a range that is empty or a revision the student did not save is 422. Anyone but the owner of the work (the teacher too) and an unknown or malformed work get 404. It says where text came from, not who wrote it.

get.summary: The comparison of a work with the thresholds of its faculty: one entry per kind that HAS a threshold, in the order of the closed list, each in_line (the share is at or below the threshold), for_review (above a soft threshold) or exceeded (above a hard threshold). An empty list while the faculty has no thresholds. It holds no share and no number; it is a statement of conformity with the rules of the faculty, not an assessment of the student, and it blocks nothing. The same answer for the student who owns the work and for its readers. Another's, an unknown or a malformed work returns 404.

200.description: the state per kind that has a threshold

delete.summary: Deletes the reading place; the note stays. Deleting what is not there changes nothing. Answers what the owner keeps. Only the student who owns the work; to anyone else, the mentor and the teachers of the work included, and for an unknown or malformed work it is 404.

put.summary: Writes the reading place (MK-9), replacing the earlier one: {place: {nodeId, offset}}. Answers what the owner keeps. Only the student who owns the work; to anyone else, the mentor and the teachers of the work included, and for an unknown or malformed work it is 404.

post.summary: The student who owns the work records that it restored the text of an earlier revision, exactly {fromRevision}. The server records it against the lowest later revision of the same student whose committed text is that of fromRevision and that has no record yet; the client never names that revision. Answers 200 {outcome, revision} with the revision the record is against: recorded (the revision just recorded) or already_recorded (the restore of fromRevision was recorded before and no later revision is left to record; the latest revision recorded as its restore), or 200 {outcome} with no_matching_revision (no such later revision is saved, as when the student typed before the save; nothing is recorded). A client confirms the restore only when that revision is the one it saved. A body that is not exactly this is 422. Anyone but the owner of the work, an unknown and a malformed work get 404.

The teacher of the work's assignment (its course teacher or its mentor) returns the whole submitted work to the student for revision, with a required comment and an optional new revision due date (a reminder, it never blocks). The submission stays recorded but is no longer the live one: the student edits and submits again as the next round. Only a live submission can be returned (409 otherwise). The student owner gets 403; everybody else who is not its teacher, and an unknown work, 404.

Records the current revision of the work as the one the caller has just reviewed (N-05); a later review moves it on. The revision comes from the record, never from the body (there is none).
